# HeroGPUI — llms.txt

> UI library for Rust desktop applications. HeroUI's design system,
> implemented in Rust on GPUI — Zed's GPU-accelerated UI framework.
> Every documented component, light and dark, fully typed.

## Overview

HeroGPUI implements HeroUI's design system in Rust: OKLCH semantic tokens,
layout tokens, and typed component builders for Windows, macOS and Linux.

- **Crate:** `herogpui` (the single dependency; re-exports GPUI itself)
- **Theme:** `herogpui-theme` — `ThemeProvider` global, `ActiveTheme` trait, `ThemeBuilder::components` / named recipes
  (`cx.colors()`, `cx.role(Color::Accent)`, `cx.layout()`)
- **Core:** `herogpui-core` — `Color`, `Variant`, `FieldVariant`, `Prominence`,
  `Backdrop`, `Size`, `SizeXl`, `Orientation`, `SelectionMode`, OKLCH math
- **Components:** `herogpui-components` — one module per `@heroui/*` package
- **Gallery:** `cargo run -p herogpui-gallery` or `cargo install --path gallery --locked` — living docs, the fifteen v3
  categories, theme switcher

**Scope note.** This file documents the current HeroUI design system only.
The previous major version used different names, and they do not exist here:
`content1..4` surface tokens, numbered 50–900 colour scales,
`primary`/`secondary` as colours, the `radius` prop, and the components
`Navbar`, `Image`, `User`, `Spacer`, `Code`, `Snippet`. Do not emit them.

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
herogpui = "0.12"
```

One dependency, and only one, published on crates.io (`cargo add herogpui`). `herogpui` is a facade over the GPUI crate
family: it depends on `gpui-pre` `0.3.11` and `gpui-pre-platform` `0.3.11` and
re-exports them, so `use herogpui::*;` is GPUI and `herogpui::application()`
opens the platform. Do not emit `gpui` or `gpui_platform` as dependencies of a
consuming crate, and never emit the unrelated crates.io `gpui` 0.2.2 crate.
(Zed does not publish `gpui` under that name; `gpui-pre` is a prerelease
publish of the Zed GPUI sources by crates.io user huacnlee, the gpui-kit
maintainer. HeroGPUI pins it exactly at `=0.3.11`.)

Paths and the Cargo features that carry them:

| Path | Crate | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `herogpui::*` | `gpui` | always |
| `herogpui::platform`, `herogpui::application` | `gpui_platform` | always |
| `herogpui::web` | `gpui_platform` | always, `cfg(target_family = "wasm")` only |
| `herogpui::core` | `herogpui-core` | `core` (implied by `theme`) |
| `herogpui::theme` | `herogpui-theme` | `theme` (implied by `components`) |
| `herogpui::components`, `herogpui::*` | `herogpui-components` | `components` (default) |

`test-support` forwards `gpui/test-support` and `gpui_platform/test-support`;
`profiler` forwards `gpui/profiler`; `multithreaded` forwards
`gpui_platform/multithreaded` — GPUI's multi-threaded web platform, wasm32
only (a nightly toolchain and a cross-origin-isolated page; off by default).
`serde` forwards `herogpui-theme/serde`
and is off by default: `ThemeDocument` is a sparse JSON override applied
through `ThemeBuilder`, so derived hover / soft mixes stay live. There is no assets or icons feature — the
embedded icons (the chrome path constants and the Lucide `IconName` set) live
inside `herogpui-components` and arrive with `components`.

```rust
use herogpui::*;

actions!(my_app, [Quit]);

struct MyRoot;

impl Render for MyRoot {
    fn render(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        app_focus_root(
            div().size_full().bg(cx.colors().background).text_color(cx.colors().foreground),
            window,
            cx,
        )
    }
}

fn main() {
    application().with_assets(HeroGpuiAssets).run(|cx: &mut App| {
        herogpui::init(cx); // = ThemeProvider::init(cx), light + dark
        // or ThemeProvider::init_with(Theme::dark(), cx);
        let bounds = Bounds::centered(None, size(px(1280.), px(820.)), cx);
        cx.open_window(WindowOptions { window_bounds: Some(WindowBounds::Windowed(bounds)), ..Default::default() },
            |_, cx| cx.new(|_| MyRoot)).unwrap();
    });
}
```

`use herogpui::*;` also brings GPUI's `FluentBuilder` — `.when(cond, ..)`,
`.when_some(opt, ..)`, `.when_none(..)`, `.map(..)` — into scope. GPUI keeps it in
`gpui::prelude` and not in `gpui::*`, so before 0.10.0 the root glob did not carry
it and a conditional builder had to be written as an if/else duplicating the whole
chain. It is a blanket impl over `IntoElement`, so it applies to every component
builder here as well as to `div()`.

Emit `herogpui::actions!`, not `gpui::actions!`: GPUI's own macro expands its
derive as the absolute path `gpui::Action`, which does not resolve when GPUI is
reached only through the facade. The facade re-implements it with
`$crate::Action`. Every GPUI *derive* macro (`Action`, `IntoElement`, `Render`,
`AppContext`, `VisualContext`) likewise expands to hard-coded `gpui::…` paths;
`use herogpui::*;` puts the name `gpui` in scope and they resolve. With a
selective import instead, add `use herogpui::gpui;` before deriving.

Eight names exist in both GPUI and HeroUI v3: `ColorSpace`, `FontWeight`,
`Menu`, `MenuItem`, `Orientation`, `Size`, `Surface`, `TextAlign`. At
`herogpui`'s root the HeroUI v3 spelling wins (`Size::Md`, not a width/height
pair); reach GPUI's through `gpui::` (`gpui::Size`, `gpui::FontWeight`).

`HeroGpuiAssets` embeds the `herogpui/icons/*.svg` files used by built-in
component chrome and every Lucide `IconName` (`herogpui/icons/lucide/*.svg`).
Use `HeroGpuiAssets::with_fallback(MyAppAssets)` when the app
also has assets. Wrap the window's root element with
`app_focus_root(root, window, cx)` to enable Tab traversal, focus-visible state,
and root capture handlers. The root takes the focus only while nothing in the window holds it (or the focused element has left the tree), so a view may focus its own handle while its window opens. Tab traversal consumes the browser default so DOM focus stays in the GPUI input surface. Focus rings appear only after a keyboard-control key (Tab, arrows, Enter/Space, typeahead, editing). A pointer press hides them, and Escape does not turn them on — closing a mouse-opened menu must not ring its trigger. Uniform overlay rings fit the control’s circular corner radius, including pill shapes, so the offset and glow stay even around the perimeter.

Set root bg/fg via tokens:

```rust
div().bg(cx.colors().background).text_color(cx.colors().foreground).font_family("Segoe UI")
```

Toggle: `herogpui::theme::toggle_light_dark(cx);` or `use_theme("dark", cx)` or
`set_theme(custom, cx)`. `use_theme` returns `Result<(), UnknownThemeError>`:
an id no registered theme carries (ids are case-sensitive) is refused, the
active theme stays as it was, and nothing repaints — it never panics.

Follow the OS instead: `theme::follow_system_appearance(window, cx)` — call it
once per window from its root-view constructor. It applies the current OS
appearance immediately and then switches between the registered `"light"` and
`"dark"` themes whenever the desktop does; `theme::stop_following_system_appearance(cx)`
ends it and `ThemeProvider::follows_system_appearance()` reports the mode for a
three-way Light/Dark/System setting. It is opt-in, so an app that pins one
appearance keeps it.

## Theming

Every base value is transcribed verbatim from
`packages/styles/themes/default/variables.css` in `oklch()`. Derived values use
the same `color-mix(in oklab, …)` weights the stylesheet uses.

**Base:** `background`, `foreground`, `muted`, `scrollbar`, `border`,
`separator`, `focus`, `link`, `backdrop`.

**Containers:** `surface` (`.background` / `.foreground`), `surface_secondary`,
`surface_tertiary`, `overlay` (floating panels), `segment` (segmented controls).

**Roles:** `default`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` — each a
`RoleColor` with `color`, `foreground`, and derived `hover()`, `soft()`,
`soft_hover()`, `soft_foreground()`. No numbered scales in v3.

**Fields:** `field.background`, `field.foreground`, `field.placeholder`,
`field.border`, plus `field.hover()` and `field.focus()`.

**Derived on `ThemeColors`:** `background_secondary()`, `background_tertiary()`,
`background_inverse()`, `separator_secondary()`, `separator_tertiary()`,
`role(Color)`.

**Layout:** `radius` (8px) with `radius_xs()`…`radius_4xl()` and `capped(r)` for v3's `min(32px, ..)` ceiling, `field_radius`,
`border_width`, `field_border_width`, `disabled_opacity`, `ring_offset_width`,
`spacing`, `surface_shadow` / `overlay_shadow` / `field_shadow` (all empty in
dark mode), `skeleton_animation`, `tooltip_delay_ms`, `tooltip_close_delay_ms`,
`cursor_interactive` (`CursorStyle::PointingHand` — v3's `cursor: pointer`; the
cursor every interactive control shows on hover).

HeroGPUI-only layout tokens (no upstream CSS variable; each defaults to the
literal it replaced, so a theme that ignores them renders v3's pixels):
`tabs_hover_opacity` (0.7 — the dim an unselected Tabs item takes on hover,
clamped to 0..=1), `tooltip_cooldown_ms` (500 — the warm window after the
pointer leaves a tooltip during which the next tip opens without its delay;
a per-tooltip close delay extends it),
`long_press_ms` (500 — how long `DropdownTrigger::LongPress` waits) and
`hover_fade_ms` (100 — the background fade duration; `0` resolves
immediately). All four plus `tooltip_delay_ms` / `tooltip_close_delay_ms` are
settable through `ThemeBuilder` and the sparse `ThemeDocument` JSON.

`ThemeBuilder::vibrant_palette(bool)` / the `"vibrant_palette"` JSON key port
HeroUI's opt-in `[data-vibrant-palette="true"]` block: off by default, on it
reweights the accent / success / warning / danger `*-soft-foreground` mixes to
92% role over 8% page foreground in both appearances, leaving
`--default-soft-foreground` and every other token alone.

```rust
div().bg(cx.colors().surface.background)
div().bg(cx.colors().accent.soft())
div().text_color(cx.colors().muted)
```

Custom theme — override a base token and every derived value follows:

```rust
use gpui::px;
use herogpui::core::{oklch, Color};
use herogpui::theme::{snow, Theme};

let brand = Theme::builder("brand", Theme::dark())
    .accent(oklch(0.55, 0.23, 295.0))
    .role(Color::Success, oklch(0.73, 0.19, 150.0), snow())
    .radius(px(6.))          // field_radius follows at 1.5x
    .cursor_interactive(gpui::CursorStyle::Arrow) // every control's hover cursor
    .build();
herogpui::theme::set_theme(brand, cx);
```

Roles are the typed `Color`, so a misspelt role does not compile. A role
name read from configuration parses with `"success".parse::<Color>()`
(`Color::from_token`), which returns `UnknownColorError` for an unknown
name instead of falling back to `accent`; the JSON `roles` map rejects an
unknown key the same way.

The same sparse overrides as JSON, behind the `serde` feature — derived
hover / soft mixes still go through `ThemeBuilder`:

```rust
use herogpui::ThemeDocument;

let brand = ThemeDocument::theme_from_json(r#"{
    "id": "brand",
    "base": "dark",
    "accent": "oklch(0.55 0.23 295)",
    "vibrant_palette": true
}"#).unwrap();
```

**Component themes.** Shared appearance belongs on `ThemeBuilder::components`, not
on per-call-site `sx`. Empty styles preserve stock HeroUI metrics. Renderers
read the active `ThemeProvider` every frame (not the builder's construction-time
theme):

stock defaults → `theme.components.*.defaults` → named recipes in `.recipe()`
order → explicit component builders → instance `sx`.

A missing recipe name is a no-op. `sx` is for placement, width and flex.

```rust
use herogpui::prelude::*;

let app = Theme::builder("app", Theme::light())
    .components(
        ComponentThemes::default()
            .slider(ComponentTheme::new(SliderStyle::default().radius(px(9999.))))
            .switch(ComponentTheme::new(SwitchStyle::default().radius(px(9999.))))
            .select(
                ComponentTheme::new(SelectStyle::default().variant(FieldVariant::Secondary))
                    .recipe("compact", SelectStyle::default().height(px(28.)).padding_x(px(8.))),
            )
            .menu(
                ComponentTheme::new(MenuStyle::default().panel_gap(px(0.)))
                    .recipe("compact", MenuStyle::default().row_height(px(28.)).panel_padding(px(4.)))
                    .recipe(
                        "accent",
                        MenuStyle::default()
                            .row_hover_bg(ComponentColor::Role(Color::Accent))
                            .row_hover_foreground(ComponentColor::RoleForeground(Color::Accent)),
                    ),
            )
            .button(
                ComponentTheme::new(ButtonStyle::default()).recipe(
                    "compact",
                    ButtonStyle::default().style(|el| {
                        el.h(px(28.)).px(px(10.)).text_size(px(12.)).line_height(px(16.))
                    }),
                ),
            )
            .text_field(
                ComponentTheme::new(TextFieldStyle::default())
                    .recipe("search", TextFieldStyle::default().height(px(32.)).text_size(px(13.))),
            ),
    )
    .build();
herogpui::theme::set_theme(app, cx);

Button::new("ok").label("OK").recipe("compact").recipe("muted");
```

`ComponentTheme<T>::new(defaults).defaults(T).recipe("name", style)` and
`ComponentThemes::{slider,switch,select,menu,button,text_field}`. `ComponentColor`
is a semantic token (`Role(Color::Accent)`, `Muted`, `FieldBackground`, …) or
`Literal(Hsla)` / `From<Hsla>`. `SliderStyle.radius` reaches the track, thumb
layers and caps through the same per-corner `sx` join as instance corners.
`ButtonStyle::style(|el| …)` captures sparse GPUI metrics; instance `sx` refines
over it. `ThemeBuilder::role_hover(Color, hsla)` / `accent_hover(hsla)` (and
`RoleColor::with_hover`) name a role's `*-hover` shade outright in place of the
derived mix toward its own foreground, for a design system whose hover moves the
other way; it reaches every component that hovers that role, so `Variant::Primary`
is correct by construction rather than one recipe and one converted call site at a
time. `*-soft-hover` is unaffected. Note that an instance `.variant(..)` suppresses
a recipe's `ButtonStyle::variant`, and with it that variant's *derived* hover — a
recipe that must change the hover names `hover_bg` instead, which applies whatever
variant is in force. `.recipe("name")` is on Slider, Switch, Select, Menu, Dropdown, Button,
Input, TextField and SearchField. `cx.components()` / `ActiveTheme::components()`
reads the live table. `components` is Rust-only — it is not a `ThemeDocument` JSON
key.

Color math (`herogpui-core`): `oklch(l, c, h)`, `oklcha(..)`,
`mix_oklab(a, b, t)`, `soft_mix(color, pct)`, `with_alpha`, `readable_color`.

## Prop vocabularies

**Corner radii.** v3 names a different step per component, so
`herogpui::extend` has one helper each rather than a single "control" radius:
`control_radius` (3xl, 24px — button, toggle button, avatar), `soft_radius`
(2xl, 16 — chip, menu and list rows, colour area), `small_radius` (xl, 12 —
close button, tag, link, tooltip), `key_radius` (lg, 8 — `Kbd`), `mark_radius`
(md — checkbox), `micro_radius` (xs — small progress track), `hairline_radius` (sm, 4 — separator, skeleton),
`field_radius` (12 — every form field) and `container_radius` (`min(32px, 3xl)` —
cards, the table and every floating panel; Surface carries none, upstream
`.surface` declares no radius). `.shots/design_audit.py` diffs these
against the real stylesheets. An `sx` corner refines a painted part
(slider track/fill/thumb, switch track/thumb) per corner, winning over
the part's own radius only where the override names it.

**Control heights** are v3's desktop values, 32 / 36 / 40 for sm / md / lg. Its
sheet is mobile-first (`.button` is `h-10 md:h-9`), and a desktop app is past
every breakpoint. A labelled button has no minimum width: it hugs its content, as
`.button`'s `w-fit` does.

**Number formatting.** `formatOptions` is v3's `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`;
`herogpui_core::NumberFormat` implements the subset the components use —
`NumberFormat::{decimal,percent,currency("USD"),unit("kilogram")}` with
`currency_sign`, `unit_display`, `minimum_fraction_digits`,
`maximum_fraction_digits` and `use_grouping`. Taken by `Meter`, `NumberField`,
`ProgressBar`, `ProgressCircle` and `Slider`. `locale` is not offered: choosing
separators, digit systems and currency placement per locale needs CLDR *number*
data, and `herogpui-core`, where `NumberFormat` lives, carries no ICU
dependency. The date components do carry one, which is why a calendar follows
the reader's locale and a formatted number does not.

v3 replaced v2's `variant` × `color` matrix with distinct enums:

| Enum | Values | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `Variant` | `Primary` `Secondary` `Tertiary` `Outline` `Ghost` `Danger` `DangerSoft` | Button, ButtonGroup |
| `FieldVariant` | `Primary` `Secondary` | every form control |
| `Prominence` | `Transparent` `Default` `Secondary` `Tertiary` | none: Card and Surface define their own `CardVariant`/`SurfaceVariant` |
| `Backdrop` | `Opaque` `Blur` `Transparent` | Modal, Drawer, AlertDialog |
| `Color` | `Default` `Accent` `Success` `Warning` `Danger` | components with a color role |
| `Size` | `Sm` `Md` `Lg` | most components |
| `SizeXl` | `Xs` `Sm` `Md` `Lg` `Xl` | ColorSwatch, ColorSwatchPicker |
| `SelectionMode` | `None` `Single` `Multiple` | ListBox, TagGroup, ToggleButtonGroup, Dropdown, Table, Select, Autocomplete, ComboBox |
| `Placement` | `Bottom` `BottomStart` `BottomLeft` `BottomEnd` `BottomRight` `Top` `TopStart` `TopLeft` `TopEnd` `TopRight` `Left` `LeftTop` `LeftBottom` `Right` `RightTop` `RightBottom` `Start` `StartTop` `StartBottom` `End` `EndTop` `EndBottom` | every floating panel: Popover, Dropdown, Tooltip, Select, ComboBox, Autocomplete, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, ColorPicker |
| `Orientation` | `Horizontal` `Vertical` | Separator, Toolbar, Slider, Tabs, ButtonGroup, ColorSlider, groups |
| `Weekday` | `Sun`...`Sat` | `firstDayOfWeek` on every date component |
| `VisibleDuration` | `Months(n)` `Weeks(n)` `Days(n)` | `visibleDuration` on Calendar, RangeCalendar |
| `PageBehavior` | `Visible` `Single` | how far navigation steps |
| `SelectionAlignment` | `Start` `Center` `End` | where the selection sits in the visible range |

`Placement` is the full 22-value React Aria union v3 forwards: every side in
both physical (`"bottom left"`) and logical (`"bottom start"`) spellings, plus
the logical edge aliases (`"start"`, `"end top"`, …). This port has no RTL
mode, so each logical spelling resolves to the same pixels as its
left/right twin. Motion and arrows follow the physical side; alignment is
positioning-only. The built-in overlays position their own panels; the
positioning helpers are crate-internal. A custom floating panel must go
through GPUI's `deferred(..)`, since gpui paints in tree order and `absolute`
alone does not lift a panel above later siblings.


## Render props

v3 passes values *into* a child render function. Where a monolithic builder
computes those values anyway, it hands them to a closure instead of asking the
caller to supply them — so the prop is real, just inverted:

- `Table::indicator(|SortDirection| ..)` — v3's `Table.SortableColumnHeader`
  `indicator`, handed `sortDirection`
- `Pagination::link(|page, is_active| ..)` — `Pagination.Link`, handed `isActive`
- `InputOTP::slot(|index, Option<char>| ..)` — `InputOTP.Slot`, handed `index`
- `Dropdown/Menu::item_content(|key, is_selected, is_indeterminate| ..)` —
  `Dropdown.Item`, handed `isSelected` / `isIndeterminate`
- `Slider::thumb(|index, value| ..)` — `Slider.Thumb`, handed `index`
- `TimeField::segment(|TimeSegment, text| ..)` — `TimeField.Segment`
- `DateField::segment(|FieldSegment, text| ..)` — `DateField.Segment`, covering date and optional time slots

## Controlled and uncontrolled

Every component takes the controlled prop as an `Option`, so leaving it unset
hands the state to the component, seeded from the matching `default*`:

```rust
Checkbox::new("terms").is_selected(self.agreed)    // controlled
Checkbox::new("terms").default_selected(true)      // uncontrolled

Select::new("lang", opts).is_open(self.open)       // controlled
Select::new("lang", opts).default_open(false)      // uncontrolled
Dropdown::uncontrolled(trigger, items)             // no `is_open` at all
```

The uncontrolled value lives in `Window::use_keyed_state`, keyed on the
component's id — so two uncontrolled components that share an id share their
state. `Popover`, `Accordion` and `Tooltip` therefore take an `id` purely to
tell instances apart. Pairs available: `is_selected`/`default_selected`
(Checkbox, Switch, ToggleButton), `is_open`/`default_open` (Popover, Select, ComboBox,
Autocomplete, Dropdown, DatePicker, DateRangePicker), `selected_key`/`default_selected_key`
(Tabs), `expanded_keys`/`default_expanded_keys` (Accordion),
`is_year_picker_open`/`default_year_picker_open` (Calendar, RangeCalendar),
`value`/`default_value` (RadioGroup, Select, CheckboxGroup, Slider, ColorArea,
ColorField, ColorPicker, ColorSlider, ColorSwatchPicker, Autocomplete, ComboBox,
Calendar, RangeCalendar, DatePicker, DateRangePicker, DateField, TimeField,
Input, TextField, SearchField, TextArea, NumberField),
`input_value`/`default_input_value` (ComboBox). Where the
controlled prop is itself an `Option` — `RadioGroup::value(None)` — supplying it
at all is what makes the component controlled.

For components whose value lives in a state entity, the entity constructor *is*
the uncontrolled seed: `InputState::with_value`, `NumberState::with_value`,
`CalendarState::with_selected`, `DateRangeState::with_range`,
`TimeState::with_value`.

## Validation

`validate` is a function the component runs, not something the caller
substitutes for. It returns the message to show, or `None`:

```rust
TextField::new(state)
    .validate(|v| (v.len() < 3).then(|| "At least 3 characters".into()))
    .validation_errors(["That name is taken"])   // e.g. from a server
```

`validation::resolve` fixes the precedence — the controlled `is_invalid`, then
`validationErrors`, then `validate`, with the component's own `error_message` as
the fallback rather than an addition. Available on Input, TextField, TextArea,
SearchField, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, InputOTP, ColorField, DateField and
TimeField. `Form` takes `validation_errors(ValidationErrors)` — HeroUI's
`Record<string, string | string[]>` record of server errors keyed by field
name. The form routes each name into that field's own error slot; editing a
field clears only its messages, reset hides them all, and a genuinely new
record re-arms every named field even when the content is identical (a clone
keeps the record's identity and re-arms nothing). Identity is reference
identity, as in React Stately: retain one record for as long as the response
is current and pass a clone each frame; building a fresh record per frame —
even with identical content — is a new server response and re-arms.
Unmatched names neither display nor block; fields without an error-display
path receive no routed messages, so a name can never block invisibly.

## Accessibility

gpui reports an element to a screen reader only when it has both an `.id(..)`
and a role, so the port states each control's role explicitly. The contract is
React Aria 3.51.0's, read from its hooks: a checkbox is `CheckBox` with
tri-state checked, a switch is `Switch`, a toggle button is `Button` with a
pressed state — or `RadioButton` inside a single-selection group, as
`useToggleButtonGroupItem` swaps it — a text field takes the role of its input
type, a slider is a `Group` around one `Slider` per thumb, and a progress bar
keeps its bounds while dropping its value when indeterminate.

`a11y::Name::field` performs the join `useField` performs with ids: the label
names the control, and the description plus any validation messages become its
description, so labels and messages reach assistive technology through the
existing field plumbing rather than a second set of props. `a11y::Range`
carries a numeric control's bounds, value, step and value text, clamped once.
Nothing here is a new builder — the roles and names are derived from the props
each component already takes.

The overlays follow: a modal, drawer, popover and toast card are dialogs, a
tooltip is a `Tooltip`, a dropdown's panel is a `Menu` whose rows are menu
items, and an accordion's own trigger row reports `aria-expanded`.

The collections state their structure. A list box is a `ListBox` of
`ListBoxOption`s carrying `aria-selected`; a table is a `Grid` — a `TreeGrid`
when its rows nest — with a header row of `ColumnHeader`s, a `RowGroup` body,
and `GridCell` (or `RowHeader`) cells carrying `aria-colindex`; tabs are a
`TabList` of `Tab`s over a `TabPanel`; a toolbar is a `Toolbar`, or a `Group`
when nested inside another; breadcrumbs are a `List` of `ListItem`s holding
links; pagination is a `Navigation` of buttons; a tag group is a `Grid` of
`Row`s. Set position (`aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize`) and grid counts
(`aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount`/`aria-rowindex`) appear exactly where React
Aria puts them — under virtualization, where the rendered rows are a window
onto a longer collection.

Select, ComboBox and Autocomplete report the parts they build: a `Button`
trigger with `aria-expanded`, a `ListBox` popup, `ListBoxOption` rows, and
`aria-activedescendant` on the highlighted row. `role="combobox"` is *not*
stated: React Aria puts it on the text input, and these components compose a
`crate::input::Input` whose role its own render decides.

gpui exposes no `aria-disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`,
`aria-readonly`, `aria-controls`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-haspopup`,
`aria-multiselectable`, `aria-sort` or live-region builder, and
no id-reference graph for `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`; those are
recorded as omissions in `crates/herogpui-components/src/a11y.rs`, and
`.shots/a11y_audit.py` is the gate. `ButtonGroup`, `InputGroup`,
`ProgressCircle`, `Fieldset`, `ToastViewport`, `ColorSwatch` and `Toolbar`
take an optional `.id()`: a named instance reports its node and an unnamed
one does not, because a constant id would fold two instances into one.
`Separator` is the remaining pending row — AccessKit 0.24 has no
`Role::Separator`.

Vanilla `gpui-pre` publishes no `aria-current` builder, so Breadcrumbs and
Pagination state the current page through styling and naming only; the
announcement waits on an upstream addition (tracked with the retired patches
under `docs/upstream/retired-patches/`).

## Component API pattern

All components are `#[derive(IntoElement)]` builders implementing `RenderOnce`:

```rust
Button::new("save")
    .child(icon)          // ordered children: leading icon first, then label text
    .child("Save")
    .variant(Variant::Primary)
    .size(Size::Md)
    .is_pending(true)
    .full_width(true)
    .on_press(cx.listener(|this, _, _, cx| this.save(cx)))
```

Components with an `sx` slot also implement GPUI's `Styled` trait. Direct
methods such as `.bg(..)`, `.w(..)` and `.rounded(..)` write to the same
root-only refinement as `sx`; neither styles independent child parts or
detached popovers. Both forms are applied after the variant and theme values,
and later builder calls win for properties they both set:

```rust
Button::new("save")
    .label("Save")
    .bg(gpui::rgba(0xffa500ff))
    .sx(|el| el.text_color(gpui::rgba(0x000000ff)))
```

State-driven layers a component draws itself — Button's hover fade, the
press-scale geometry — read the override's background and pixel size, so the
override holds across states too. Where that means a state stops moving —
an `sx` background freezes Button's hover fade on the override — the component
names the escape hatch (`Button::hover_bg`).

Controlled state lives in your entity (`InputState`, `CalendarState`,
`TimeState`, `NumberState`, `OtpState`, `DateRangeState`):

```rust
let name = cx.new(|cx| InputState::new(cx));
TextField::new(name.clone()).label("Name").is_required(true)
```

Callbacks: `Fn(&ClickEvent/&str/f32/usize/bool/Option<Date>, &mut Window, &mut App)`.
Fields cloned into closures must be `Arc`.

Public surface (0.12): the component builders and their payload types live at
the crate root; `anim` (motion tokens and wrappers) is a module path, not
re-exported at the root; `extend` holds the helpers supported for custom
widgets (the radius scale, `FIELD_*` metrics, `cursor_interactive`,
`focus_visible`/`set_focus_visible`, `inner_fill_radius`,
`shift_wheel_scroll_x`, `app_focus_root`); the old `util` module is private.
Theme structs (`Theme`, `ThemeColors`, `LayoutTheme`, `ComponentThemes`, the
`*Style` recipes), `TabItem`, and every render-prop payload (`*RenderState`,
`*CellState`, `InteractiveState`, `FieldFocus`, `SelectionValue`, …) are
`#[non_exhaustive]`: build them with their constructors, builders or
`Default`, then set fields — never with a struct literal.

Entity-backed controls derive internal identity from their state entity. Keep a
distinct `InputState`, `CalendarState`, `DateRangeState` or `TimeState` for each
simultaneously rendered control, and retain that entity across repaints.
Cloning a handle shares the same state and identity. To synchronize two controls,
give each its own entity and synchronize their values through the owner.

## Components

This file documents every component HeroUI v3.2.7 ships. Entries are grouped
so a few cover a component together with its group or slot siblings, two
entries (`PickerColor`, `DateConstraints`) describe shared helpers rather
than standalone components, and `Scrollbar` is a HeroGPUI extension with no
HeroUI counterpart. The gallery and website likewise give a few sibling
components a shared page (`toggle-button`, `disclosure`, `label-messages`).

v3 keeps `size` on nineteen components (Button, ButtonGroup, ToggleButton*,
Chip, TagGroup, Badge, Avatar, Switch, Meter, ProgressBar, ProgressCircle,
Spinner, Pagination, Modal, AlertDialog, ScrollShadow, ColorSwatch*) and gives
every form field one height instead — `extend::FIELD_HEIGHT` / `FIELD_TEXT` /
`FIELD_ICON`. `color` survives only on Avatar, Badge, Chip, ColorSwatch*, Meter,
ProgressBar, ProgressCircle, Spinner and Typography; elsewhere `variant` (or
`status`, on Alert) is the whole visual vocabulary. `CloseButton` has neither.

### Buttons
`Button`, `ToggleButton` and `CloseButton` reconcile explicit pixel `sx` corners on their painted skins and hover fills, with each specified corner winning over `radius`. Press geometry scales those corners individually; unmentioned grouped corners keep their group-edge shape.

- **Button** — `variant(Variant)`, `size`, `full_width`, `is_icon_only`, `radius(px)`, `recipe("name")` (stacks `Theme.components.button` recipes), `is_disabled`, `is_pending`, `aria_label(text)`, ordered children (the icons and label text are children in order, matching v3 — there are no start/end content slots), `on_press` `aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `hover_bg(Hsla)` names the fill the hover fade eases *to*. v3 has no such prop — on the web it is `className="hover:bg-…"` — and it exists because an `sx` background alone pins both of the fade's endpoints (a fade back to the variant colour would paint over the override), leaving a custom surface with no hover. With it the fade runs from the resting background (the `sx` one when set, the variant's otherwise) to the named colour, on the same timing. Pressing uses the pinned variant `--button-bg-pressed` endpoint inside the size-specific scaled skin; it does not dim the whole button with opacity.
  - `width(px)`, `min_width(px)`, `height(px)`, `padding_x(px)`, `text_size(px)`, `font_weight(FontWeight)` and `grow(bool)` are per-component repository extensions in the `radius` mould — not v3 props — naming the box and the label without an `sx` workaround. Each beats what `size` derives: `height` and `padding_x` replace the control-height and `px-4`/`px-3` rungs, `text_size` re-pairs its leading through the Tailwind step table, `font_weight` replaces `font-medium`; a matching `sx` override still refines the root last, and the pressed skin keeps the fixed box instead of snapping back to the ladder. An explicit pixel `width` wins over `full_width` and the icon-only square. `grow(true)` is v3's `flex-1` plus `min-w-0`: the button shares the row's free width and may compress below its content width, composing with `full_width`.
- **ButtonGroup** — `id()`, `variant`, `size`, `orientation`, `button(Button)` (members inherit), `is_disabled`, `full_width`. A named group reports `role="group"`.
- **CloseButton** — `aria_label(text)` overrides the localized accessible name; `is_disabled`, `radius(px)`, `icon(el)`, `content(|state| el)`, `on_press`, `hover_bg(color)` (v3's `variant` has one value, so there is nothing to select and no builder for it). `hover_bg` is additive, matching `Button::hover_bg`: the fade rests on the `sx` background when set, else `--default`, and eases to the named colour. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the box is the button's whole shape, so the pressed box scales the resolved value instead of snapping back to the helper.
- **ToggleButton / ToggleButtonGroup** — `is_selected`, `aria_label(text)`, `variant(ToggleVariant::{Default,Ghost})`, `size`, `hover_bg(color)`, `radius(px)`, `selection_mode`, `is_detached`, `orientation`, `full_width`, `ToggleSeparator`. Both apply v3's `scale(0.97)` press. `hover_bg` follows the same resting-endpoint contract as `Button::hover_bg`; `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius` and a group edge still rounds only the member's outer corners.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `ToggleButton::on_change(&bool)` reports the selection a press moves to, alongside `on_press`. A button's selection key is `key()` when given, otherwise its element id, so a group can namespace child ids without breaking selection.

### Collections
Cmd-vs-Ctrl conventions (select-all, the Home/End chords) follow the runtime
platform — `App::platform_info()` — so the web build on a Mac uses Cmd.

- **Dropdown** — `Dropdown::new(trigger, items, is_open).placement(Placement).on_open_change(&bool).on_action(&str).row_hover_bg(color).radius(px).recipe("name")` (stacks `Theme.components.menu` recipes onto the menu and its submenus), `MenuItem::new(key,label).shortcut().icon().danger().is_interactive(bool)`, `MenuItem::SectionLabel`, `MenuItem::Separator`. `separator_inset(px)` / `separator_thickness(px)` on `Menu` (and `MenuStyle`) give the `Separator` rule a per-edge inset and an explicit thickness, for a panel sitting beside a native menu whose own rule is inset inside wider panel bounds; unset keeps v3's own proportional rule — the rule sits 3% in from each edge at 94% of the panel width — not a full-bleed hairline. `is_interactive(true)` hands the row's interaction to the element `item_content` draws for it — HeroUI's inline secondary-control rows, where the trailing control is a small select or stepper rather than a submenu flyout. It drops the row-level click, its action and dismissal, the `[data-pressed]` scale, and Enter/Space activation, while keeping the row a keyboard stop with its hover fill, focus ring, `menuitem` role and name. A popup opened from inside such a row needs no extra plumbing: it registers on the shared overlay stack, which makes it topmost, and the menu's outside-press and Escape dismissals already stand down for anything above them. `item_start_content(|key, InteractiveState| -> Option<AnyElement>)` on `Dropdown`, `Menu` and `ContextMenu` (HeroGPUI extension) draws a caller element as a row's leading content, in place of `MenuItem::icon`'s asset path; `None` keeps the item's icon, and submenus inherit the closure. `MenuItem::Item` is `#[non_exhaustive]` — build rows through `MenuItem::new` and its builders, which cover every field. Built-in labels use 14px/20px medium text, descriptions and section headers use 12px/16px, and shortcut hints render as light `Kbd`. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the menu panel's entry zoom interpolates the override; an item's own `rounded-2xl` mark is an inner part and keeps its step. A closed `Press` trigger opens on Enter, Space and ArrowDown with the first enabled row highlighted, and on ArrowUp with the last; Alt+ArrowDown and Alt+ArrowUp do the same, and a `LongPress` trigger opens from the keyboard only through Alt+Enter, Alt+Space and the Alt+Arrow chords (React Aria's `useMenuTrigger`). A menu with a selection mode opens with its first enabled selected row highlighted instead, including a pointer open, which otherwise highlights nothing.
  - Standalone `Menu::new(id, items)` can be embedded in a tray or caller-positioned popup. `recipe("name")` stacks `Theme.components.menu` recipes. `focus_handle(handle)` supplies the root handle; `on_dismiss(|refocus: &bool, window, cx| ..)` lets the owner remove the menu. `false` means a keyboard pick must not immediately refocus a clickable trigger. `panel_min_width`, `panel_max_width`, `panel_max_height`, `row_height` (minimum), `row_padding_x`, `row_padding_y`, `row_text_size`, `row_gap`, `panel_gap` (default 2px between entries), and `panel_padding` accept pixels and reach painted parts. Compact: 28px row / 8px x / 2px y / 12px text / 8px gap / 4px panel. Normal app styling: 36px / 10px / 6px / 14px / 12px / 6px. Unset keeps stock standalone defaults (36 / 8 / 6 / 14 / 12 / 4). `animate_entry(false)` suppresses entry motion. `row_hover_foreground(color)` pairs with `row_hover_bg` for hovered/focused/open-submenu rows, including built-in shortcut and icon colors; disabled rows keep their treatment. Presentation, action/dismissal and render callbacks propagate to submenus; selection remains scoped to each menu, as in the stock implementation; their own focus returns to the parent on Left/Escape. `sx` still styles the outer wrapper.

  The menu positions against the measured trigger: all 22 union placements
  flip to the side with more room when the preferred side cannot fit, keep a
  12px cross-axis viewport inset, and cap the scroller to the available height
  with short menus keeping their natural height.
  Submenus position independently against their row end top and flip sides to
  the side with more room when needed; the parent stays anchored and outside
  presses still dismiss the whole menu.
  Descriptions wrap within the popover width; long menus remain scrollable.
  - selection: `selection_mode(SelectionMode)`, `selected_keys`, `disabled_keys`, `on_selection_change(&[SharedString])`, `on_action(&str)`. Selected items draw a check; disabled ones are muted and inert. The next selection comes from `selection::next_selection`, shared with ToggleButtonGroup and Table.
- **ListBox** — `ListBox::new(id, items).selection_mode().selected_keys().disabled_keys().escape_key_behavior(EscapeKeyBehavior::{ClearSelection,None}).max_h().row_hover_bg(color).on_selection_change().on_action()`, `ListBoxItem::new(key,label).description().icon().shortcut().danger()`, `::section()`, `::separator()`. Built-in labels use 14px/20px medium text, descriptions and section headers use 12px/16px, and shortcut hints render as light `Kbd`. Enabled rows use HeroUI's subtle `0.98` pressed scale with the pinned 250ms `ease-out-quart` transition inside a stable footprint, while custom `item_content` also receives `is_pressed`. Selected/custom indicators occupy an absolute 16px inline-end slot with 28px reserved end padding, so long labels do not push the marker through flex layout. Fixed-row virtual lists cap at `max_h`, shrink below it in a bounded parent, and page by the visible viewport, including after resize, while skipping disabled stops.
- **TagGroup** — `TagGroup::new(id, tags).full_width(bool).label().selection_mode().selected_keys().escape_key_behavior(EscapeKeyBehavior::{ClearSelection,None}).size().radius(px).variant(TagVariant::{Default,Surface}).hover_bg(color).remove_hover_bg(color).empty_state().on_remove().on_selection_change()`, `Tag::new(key,label).icon().remove_content(render)`. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the size step (`rounded-xl`, `rounded-2xl` on `Lg`) stays the fallback, and the remove button inside a chip is an inner part that stays a circle. Removal uses a 24px pointer target around the 12px glyph and layout slot, matching HeroUI 3.2.5 without widening the tag.
  Small/medium tags set 12px text with 16px leading; large tags set 14px text
  with 20px leading. Labels, descriptions, and empty states also set their own
  line height, so inherited leading does not change tag heights.

### Colors
ColorSlider labels/output, ColorPicker triggers, and ColorField display text use 14px text with a 20px line height independent of their parent.
- **PickerColor** — shared value: `from_hex`, `to_hex`, `from_rgb`, `to_rgb`, `to_hsla`, `channel()`, `with_channel()`, `with_alpha()`
- **ColorArea** — `ColorArea::new(id, value)`; `color_space(ColorSpace)` sets both axes to that space's channel pair, `x_channel` / `y_channel` override either, `size(w,h)`, `show_dots` (the dot-grid overlay), `is_disabled`, `on_change`, `on_change_end`
- **ColorField** — `ColorField::new(id, Option<PickerColor>)`; concrete `PickerColor` values still convert directly, while `None` is HeroUI's documented empty `Color | null` state. `default_value(Option<PickerColor>)` seeds an uncontrolled concrete or empty field; the outer Rust `Option` distinguishes an omitted builder from an explicit null seed. `channel(ColorChannel)`, `color_space(ColorSpace)`, `label`, `aria_label(text)`, `description`, `variant`, `full_width`, `radius(px)`, the validity flags. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and both of its boxes follow it: the static display box sets the resolved value back over the shared field chrome, and the editable path forwards it to the inner `Input` it renders. `sx(|s| ..)` refines the root column (label, box and description or error) on both paths: the editable field hands it to the `Input` it composes, whose standalone root is that column, and the static display refines its own; the box keeps its chrome. A `content` render closure replaces the whole field and takes no `sx`, as on the other fields.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `full_width(true)` expands both the outer wrapper and control to the available parent width.
  - `state(Entity<InputState>)` makes it **editable**; without one it is a read-only display of `value`. `placeholder`, and `on_change(&Option<PickerColor>)` reporting `None` when the text is not a colour, exactly as v3 types it. With a `channel` the text is that channel's number rather than a hex value.
  - Focus loss commits the field the way React Aria chains `onBlur: commit`: text that no longer parses to a colour restores the formatted last-committed value, valid typed text stays exactly as typed, and an emptied field stays empty (its committed null) — with no `on_change` fired for the rejected text. The revert is built in, and `on_blur(|window, cx| ..)` hooks the focus loss itself, firing ahead of the revert the way React Aria chains the caller's `onBlur` ahead of `commit`. Editable mode only.
- **ColorPicker** — `label`, `is_open`, `show_alpha`, `font_family(name)`, `on_change`, `on_open_change`
  - When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset and an 8px trigger gap, and its scroller caps to the available height so taller control stacks scroll vertically; Tab moves through area/hue/alpha and reveals each focused control.
- **ColorSlider** — `ColorSlider::new(id, value, channel).color_space(ColorSpace).orientation().length().show_label().aria_label(text).on_change().on_change_end()` `aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `color_space` is not cosmetic: HSL and HSB saturation are different quantities for the same colour, so a saturation slider reads and writes through `PickerColor::{channel_in, with_channel_in}`. Every other channel is space-independent.
  - Gradient, endpoint colors, and alpha checkerboard stay inside the rounded track in both orientations. The thumb and focus ring remain outside that clip.
  - The gradient spans the thumb's travel between the 10px end caps. Caps match its endpoint colors; hue uses the saturated spectrum, and only the alpha track displays transparency.
  - Track edges use one-pixel unblurred inset shadows, including the rounded caps, without a separate solid outline.
- `ColorSwatchPicker::sx(|el| ..)` styles the group layout, including gap, width and wrapping. Built-in swatches follow their allocated cell size; grid keyboard navigation uses the rendered width, and a non-wrapping group has one row.
- **ColorSwatch** — `ColorSwatch::new(color)`, `id()`, `color_name(text)`, `size(SizeXl)`, `shape(SwatchShape::{Circle,Square})`. A named swatch reports `role="img"`; it uses the canonical hex as its accessible name unless `color_name` supplies a human-readable override.
- **ColorSwatchPicker** — `value`, `size`, `shape`, `layout(SwatchLayout::{Grid,Stack})`, `on_change`

### Controls
- **Slider** — `Slider::new(id, value).value().default_value().min_value().max_value().step().orientation().size(SliderSize).label().aria_label(text).show_value().format_options().recipe("name").on_change(&f32).on_change_end(&f32)`. `recipe` stacks `Theme.components.slider` overlays; a theme `radius` reaches the track, thumb layers and caps, with instance `sx` corners still winning per corner. The multi-thumb form is `values(Vec<f32>)` + `on_change_all(&[f32])`; dragging moves whichever thumb is nearest, and `thumb(|index, value|)` is v3's `Slider.Thumb` render prop. `size(SliderSize)` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` (the default) is v3's geometry — a 20px rail, a 28x20-around-24x16 two-layer thumb and a 12px axis inset — while `Sm` is a 6px pill rail with an 8px inset and a single 12px round knob in the foreground colour. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `Slider::show_steps(true)` draws optional decorative 3px step dots (at most 1,000). `Slider::marks([SliderMark::new(0.), SliderMark::new(50.).child("Half"), SliderMark::new(100.)])` adds labels at arbitrary values without changing snapping. Empty marks use `format_options`; invalid or out-of-range marks are omitted. Indicators follow the selected interval, the orientation, and RTL chrome locales. Horizontal RTL also reverses pointer and left/right keys; vertical values still grow upward.
  - Native seek extensions: `continuous(true)` disables pointer snapping and uses 1% arrow / 10% page keyboard increments. `steps(iter)` snaps to sorted, deduplicated finite points inside min/max; arrows visit adjacent points and ties choose the lower point. No usable points falls back to continuous movement. `step`, `continuous` and `steps` replace the preceding mode; stock remains `step(1.0)`. `on_drag_start(|window, cx| ..)` precedes the first pointer write; `on_drag_end(|window, cx| ..)` follows `on_change_end` on left release, including outside the track and unchanged clicks. Keyboard changes only call the change callbacks. Single-thumb mode allocates no unused range value state. Pixel corners supplied by `sx` reach the track, fill, edge caps and both Md thumb layers; `sx(|el| el.rounded_full())` rounds the painted perimeter. Joined single-thumb cap/fill edges stay square under supplied corners; no-sx and range fill geometry is unchanged.

- **Switch** — `is_selected`, `size`, `control_scale(f32)` (positive finite scale for the painted track and thumb, preserving layout and label metrics), `hover_bg(color)`, `recipe("name")` (stacks `Theme.components.switch` overlays; theme `radius` reaches the clipped track and thumb), `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`, `is_required`, `label(el)`, `aria_label(text)`, `on_change(&bool)` / `on_press`. The focusable switch-content row owns the single toggle target, so its label and track both activate once; the thumb travels for 300ms while its color eases for 200ms, and reduced motion snaps both. v3's `value` is the form-submission value, not the state, so there is no builder for it. Content uses 14px text with 20px lines; the built-in label is the shared `.label` part, 14px medium text with 20px lines. `text_size(px)` replaces the label's (and `content` row's) `text-sm` (a 12/14/16px size takes v3's 16/20/24 leading and any other keeps 20px); the track, thumb and description keep their metrics (a HeroGPUI extension).A plain-string `label("…")` names a Checkbox or Switch on its own; a composed label element needs `aria_label`.

### Data Display
- **Badge** — `BadgeAnchor::new()` is v3's `Badge.Anchor`, the positioning wrapper whose children are the anchored element plus the `Badge::new().variant(BadgeVariant::{Primary,Secondary,Soft}).color().size().text_size(px).radius(px).placement(BadgePlacement)` composed as a later child. `BadgeLabel::new()` is the `px-0.5` text slot — v3 auto-wraps plain text children in it, which GPUI cannot intercept, so the wrap is explicit. No children on the badge is v3's dot badge, and the page-background ring stays unconditional. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the size step (`small_radius`/`control_radius`/`soft_radius`) stays the fallback, so an un-overridden badge keeps its step.
- **Chip** — `Chip::new().variant(ChipVariant::{Primary,Secondary,Tertiary,Soft}).color().size().text_size(px).radius(px)` renders arbitrary ordered children verbatim (an icon, a dot, a `ChipLabel`, a trailing element); `ChipLabel::new()` is the `px-0.5` text slot for the label text. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, replacing the chip's default `soft_radius` step. A removable chip is `TagGroup`, which is where v3 puts `onRemove`.
- **Table** — `Table::new(columns).row(cells).variant(TableVariant::{Primary,Secondary}).row_hover_bg(color).radius(px).on_row_click(&usize, &ClickEvent)` — `variant` is the whole visual story in v3; `isStriped`/`isBordered` were v2. Headers use 12px/16px text; body cells use 14px/20px text in ordinary and virtual rows. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, replacing the wrapper shell's default; the `Primary` tray paints its own radius over that shell exactly as it covers the default, so the override shows where the default does (`Secondary`).
  - Horizontal wheel input scrolls columns; vertical input does not shift them sideways.
  - Tree rows use `tree_column(index)` for the chevron column; its start padding follows HeroUI's `1rem * (aria-level)` rule, so each nested level advances 16px in both the painted cell and its measured intrinsic track.
  - columns: `column(TableColumn::new("Name").allows_sorting(true).is_row_header(true))`. `is_row_header` has no a11y layer to reach, so it renders that column's cells in medium weight.
  - selection: `selection_mode`, `selection_behavior(SelectionBehavior::{Toggle,Replace})`, `selected_keys`, `default_selected_keys`, `disallow_empty_selection`, `on_selection_change(&[SharedString])`, `keyed_row(key, cells)` (a row's key defaults to its index). Adds a checkbox column, with select-all in the header for `Multiple`; replace behavior selects the focused row and makes a plain activation the sole selection, while explicit checkboxes still toggle and `disallow_empty_selection` protects the final key.
  - sorting: `sort_descriptor(SortDescriptor::new(col, SortDirection::Ascending))`, `on_sort_change`, `show_indicator`. `SortDescriptor::next` gives the descriptor a header click should produce — flip the sorted column, start any other ascending. **The table never reorders its own rows**: a row is already-rendered cells, so the caller sorts its data and rebuilds.
  - keyboard: PageUp moves from the body to the first column header — from the top of a virtual body; mid-body it pages by the visible viewport. Enter/Space sorts a sortable header; Down/PageDown returns to the first/last enabled row. Unsortable headers remain outside the Tab order and preserve their configured column widths.
  - virtualization: with `row_height` + `virtual_rows`, the fixed-row body caps at `max_h`, shrinks below it in a bounded parent, and PageUp/PageDown move by the visible viewport, including after resize, while skipping disabled stops.
  - resizing: `TableColumn::allows_resizing(true).default_width(px(..)).min_width(px(..)).max_width(px(..))`; use `width(px(..))` plus `Table::on_resize` for controlled widths. `on_resize_start` / `on_resize` / `on_resize_end` receive the known `(column label, pixel width)` map for pointer and keyboard resizing.
  - `empty_state(el)` for `renderEmptyState`; `is_pending(bool)` + `on_load_more(fn)` for the scroll-intersection load-more sentinel.
  - HeroGPUI extensions (not v3 props): column reordering and cell selection, see **Table data extras** under HeroGPUI extensions.

### Date and Time
- **DateConstraints** — shared by all five: `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_date_unavailable(fn)`, `first_day_of_week(Weekday)`, `weeks_in_month`. Each component takes them individually, or a whole set via `.constraints(..)`. The default first weekday comes from the operating system's regional date preferences and ICU4X's compiled CLDR week data; invalid or unavailable preferences fall back to Sunday, and `first_day_of_week` remains an explicit override. The month grid's own text follows the same preference: the month and weekday names, and the order of the year-and-month heading, come from ICU4X's compiled CLDR (a Japanese reader gets a year-first heading, not a translated template), falling back to English when CLDR does not know the reported locale. On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` there is no operating system to ask -- `system_locale` has no browser regional-locale reader -- so a calendar compiled for the web always draws that English fallback, whatever the visitor's browser language.
- **Calendar** — `CalendarState::new(cx)`, `Calendar::new(state).value(..).is_disabled().is_read_only().is_invalid().day_hover_bg(color).nav_hover_bg(color).year_hover_bg(color).focused_value().on_focus_change().on_change(&Option<Date>)` plus the constraints. The `locale(tag)` Unicode calendar extension selects the grid system; month/year navigation, bounds and alignment use that system, while values and callbacks stay Gregorian. Today uses the accent-soft fill/foreground, selected and pressed endpoints use the pinned accent colors, and unavailable/out-of-range cells use muted disabled opacity with an operation-not-allowed cursor; unavailable dates remain keyboard-focusable but pointer-inert. Enabled navigation buttons interpolate their hover fill over the pinned 100ms ease-out transition and retain the deep press scale.
-  The built-in year-picker trigger keeps one down chevron and rotates it 90° over 150ms when opened; reduced motion settles it immediately.
- **DateField** — three editable date segments in the operating system's regional order and separators, plus optional time segments in the regional order, separators, padding, and localized day-period names, with click-to-focus, arrow steppers that roll over month and year correctly, and the `segment(|FieldSegment, text|)` render prop. `locale(tag)` overrides that regional format (v3's `I18nProvider`). The ISO text stays in the bound `InputState`, so `name`, `FormField::text` and `on_change` are unchanged. `DateField::new(InputState).locale().label().full_width().is_required().is_invalid().font_family(name).variant().placeholder_value().should_force_leading_zeros(true).radius(px).value(Option<Date>).on_change(&Option<Date>)`; month, day and hour padding can be forced to two digits. Enabled, unfocused fields interpolate their hover fill over the pinned 150ms ease-smooth transition while focus, invalid and disabled chrome keep precedence. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the field box and shared chrome use the resolved radius, while the segments retain their own `rounded-md` marks.
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
  - constraints: `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_date_unavailable`, or `constraints(DateConstraints)`. The three ways a typed date can be wrong — unparseable, out of range, unavailable — report as distinct messages, and `on_change` yields `None` for a date the constraints reject, so a caller never receives a value it said it would not accept.
- **DatePicker** — `DatePicker::new(CalendarState).label().locale().is_open().on_open_change().value().is_disabled().is_invalid().placement(Placement).on_change()` plus the constraints; `placement` accepts the shared 22-value `herogpui_core::Placement` vocabulary and defaults to centered `Bottom`, matching HeroUI's `Popover.placement="bottom"` and its default 8px trigger gap. `locale` is forwarded to the embedded field and the popover calendar. State and form data remain ISO-formatted. Popover entry uses keyed 150ms ease-smooth fade/zoom-in-95 with a placement slide; the shared positioner flips to the opposite physical side when needed. Closing retains the panel for the 100ms zoom-out-95/fade exit and gates calendar interaction while it leaves. A true short-viewport max-height cap and pointer-events suppression remain limited by the native overlay API. A calendar pick always replaces the field text, including a typed date the picker rejected (out of range or unavailable).
- **DateRangePicker** — `DateRangeState::new(cx)`, `DateRangePicker::new(state).label().placeholder().size().is_open().is_disabled().placement(Placement).trigger_hover_bg(color).is_invalid().on_open_change(&bool).on_change()`, plus the `DateConstraints` setters; `placement` defaults to centered `Bottom` and accepts the full shared placement vocabulary with the default 8px trigger gap. Both embedded date fields use the operating system's regional date format while state and form data remain ISO-formatted. The range popover follows the same keyed placement slide, 150ms entry, opposite-side flip and retained 100ms exit contract; a true short-viewport max-height cap and pointer-events suppression remain limited by the native overlay API. A completed calendar range always replaces both field texts, including a typed date the picker rejected.
  - the popover renders `RangeCalendar`, so the hover preview between the anchor and the cursor, the constraint treatments and the year picker all come along.
- **RangeCalendar** — `RangeCalendar::new(DateRangeState).value(start, end).allows_non_contiguous_ranges().day_hover_bg(color).nav_hover_bg(color).year_hover_bg(color).focused_value().on_focus_change().on_change(start, end)` plus the constraints. During a contiguous selection, `is_date_unavailable` receives the first endpoint and derives temporary cell, focus and navigation bounds by scanning through one visible duration on each side plus the sentinel day beyond each limit; non-contiguous mode removes those interior bounds while unavailable endpoints remain inert. `locale(tag)` uses the same calendar-system conversions for the grid, paging, year picker and unavailable-range scan. Day buttons use 14px/20px medium text in all states; custom `cell` content inherits these metrics. Today uses the accent-soft fill/foreground, range endpoints use accent colors and unavailable/out-of-range cells use muted disabled opacity with an operation-not-allowed cursor; unavailable dates remain keyboard-focusable but pointer-inert. Enabled navigation buttons interpolate their hover fill over the pinned 100ms ease-out transition and retain the deep press scale.
-  The built-in year-picker trigger uses the same single down-chevron and 90°/150ms rotation contract.
- **TimeField** — `TimeState::with_value(cx, Time::new(9,30))`, `TimeField::new(state).value().min_value().max_value().placeholder_value().hour_cycle(HourCycle::{H12,H24}).should_force_leading_zeros(true).show_seconds().stepper_hover_bg(color).font_family(name).radius(px).on_change(&Option<Time>)`; without explicit overrides, `TimeField` and time-granularity `DateField` use the system regional segment order, literals, numeric padding, localized day-period names, and 12/24-hour cycle, while an empty time starts at midnight. Enabled, unfocused fields interpolate their hover fill over the pinned 150ms ease-smooth transition while focus, invalid and disabled chrome keep precedence. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: the field box and shared chrome use the resolved radius, while the segments keep their own `rounded-md` and the steppers their fixed 4px corners.
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
  - `full_width(true)` expands both the outer wrapper and control to the available parent width.

### Feedback
- **Alert** — `Alert::new(title).description().description_content(el).status(Color).radius(px)` plus composed children (v3 spells it `status`, removed `variant`/`radius`, and removed `isClosable`/`onClose` — a close affordance is an ordinary child, e.g. a composed `CloseButton`). `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it replaces the root's default `--radius-3xl` (capped).
- **Meter** — `Meter::new(id, value).value().min_value().max_value().value_label().label().show_value().color().size().radius(px)`. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, forwarded to the bar the meter delegates its track to — the same ride-along as the `sx` slot — so it replaces that bar's size-step radius.
- **ProgressBar** — `ProgressBar::new(id)`, then `value`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `value_label`, `is_indeterminate`, `size`, `color`, `radius(px)`, `label`, `show_value_label`, `format_options(NumberFormat)`. Labels and outputs use 14px text with a fixed 20px line height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`: the size still picks the default, and the override replaces it for the track and every fill segment inside it.
- **ProgressCircle** — `id()`, `value`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `is_indeterminate`, `color`, `size(Size)` (32/48/64px), `show_value_label`. A named ring reports `role="progressbar"`. The ring weight is 10% of the diameter, as v3 scales it with `size`.
- **Skeleton** — `id`, `w`, `h`, `radius(px)`, `animation_type(SkeletonAnimation::{Shimmer,Pulse,None})` (defaults to `--skeleton-animation`). v3 renders the skeleton *or* the content, so there is no `isLoaded`. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, replacing the near-square `rounded-sm` default.
- **Spinner** — `size(SpinnerSize::{Sm,Md,Lg,Xl})`, `size_px(Pixels)` for the in-between diameters the size steps do not cover (the explicit override wins over `size` in either builder order), `color`, `current_color(Hsla)` for `color="current"` (gpui svgs do not inherit text colour), optional `duration_ms` for deterministic speed variants, and `glyph(impl IntoElement)` to replace the arc with a caller element — the spinner keeps owning the box, applies the resolved colour to the glyph the same way it colours the arc, and keeps the same rotation, reduced-motion suppression and `role="status"` "Loading" root; pass the `svg()` element itself, since gpui transforms only svgs. The default follows HeroUI's 750ms `animate-spin-fast` token; the diameter does not shrink in flex layouts; the app reduced-motion preference stops rotation.

### Calendar view model (`calendar_view`)

`Calendar` and `RangeCalendar` show a month grid, several month grids side by
side, a run of week rows, or a rolling window of days. Day cells, month headings and
year cells use 14px/20px medium text; weekday labels use 12px/16px medium text.
Headers have 16px bottom padding, weekday labels have 8px bottom padding, and
date rows start 4px below the weekday block. Calendar rows are contiguous;
RangeCalendar retains 2px vertical cell margins.
Calendar single-month, week and day rows use seven 36px columns without horizontal gaps, aligned
with their weekday headings.
Multiple-month views use 256px panels separated by 32px, with square cells one
seventh of the panel width and horizontal scrolling when the host is narrower.
Day views retain seven weekday columns, render dates before the requested start
as disabled, and leave blank cells after its end. Navigation still uses the
requested day count.
The year picker overlays the retained day area without changing the view dimensions.
Its year list scrolls independently and reveals the active row on opening, keyboard
navigation, or a date-bound change that moves that year to another row.

- `visible_duration(VisibleDuration::Months(2) | Weeks(2) | Days(5))`
- `page_behavior(PageBehavior::Visible | Single)` — step the whole range or one unit
- `selection_alignment(SelectionAlignment::Start | Center | End)` — applied until
  the user navigates or picks, after which the state pins the displayed range.
  Picking from an initially aligned view preserves its month/week/day anchor.
  `Center` matches React Aria: it halves the duration and then backs off again on
  an even count, so a 2-up range aligns like `Start`.
- `year_picker(bool)` — composes v3's `YearPickerTrigger`: the heading becomes
  the interactive year-picker control (with its rotating chevron) instead of a
  plain label. `is_year_picker_open(bool)` and `default_year_picker_open(bool)`
  imply it, since a picker state with no trigger could never open.
  `on_year_picker_open_change(fn)` reports the trigger's open changes.

The geometry is pure and testable: `calendar_view::{page, aligned_anchor,
week_start, month_headings, linear_cells, range_heading, year_page}`.

### Forms
- **Input** — `InputState {value,cursor,anchor,focus_handle}`, `variant(FieldVariant)`, `label`, `aria_label(text)`, `placeholder`, `description`, `error_message`, `start/end_content`, `full_width`, `text_size(px)`, `radius(px)`, `recipe("name")` (stacks `Theme.components.text_field` recipes), `is_clearable`, `clear_hover_bg(color)`, `is_required`, `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`, `on_change(&str)`, `on_submit(&str)`. Text adornments inherit the field's 14px text and 20px line height. Labels use 14px/20px and descriptions/errors use 12px/16px, independent of host leading. Platform text replacement, composition updates, and paste preserve selection, filtering, and change callbacks. Enter during composition does not submit the field.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `input_type(InputType::{Text,Password,Email,Number,Tel,Url,Search})` — `Password` masks, `Number` filters keystrokes
  - `max_length` (enforced while typing), `min_length`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `pattern(fn)`
  - `validity(&str) -> InputValidity` — a pure query; feed the result back through `is_invalid` / `error_message`
  - `height(px)` — replaces the 36px box height. Only the row height changes: the text keeps its 14px size and 20px line and stays centred. The multi-line surface (`TextArea`) takes its own `height(px)` floor instead — see below.
  - `padding_x(px)` — replaces the box's 12px (`px-3`) horizontal padding. Inside an `InputGroup` the group owns the padding, so it is ignored there.
  - `is_bare(bool)` — renders the box with no background, border, field shadow or focus/invalid ring: the same chrome-less treatment `InputGroup.Input` already gets, for a field the caller paints around. Focus, editing and the invalid state itself are unchanged.
  - `focus_ring(bool)` — GPUI extension that hides only the visual focus ring when `false`; the field remains focusable and editable, and invalid feedback remains visible. The same switch is available on `TextField`, `TextArea`, `SearchField`, `InputGroup`, `Select`, `ComboBox`, `Autocomplete`, `NumberField`, `TimeField`, `DateField` and `ColorField`.
  - Theme default: `TextFieldStyle::default().focus_ring(false)` inside `ComponentTheme::new(...)` applies the shared default to `Input`, `TextField`, `TextArea` and `SearchField`; an instance `.focus_ring(...)` override wins over the theme.
  - `font_family(name)` — the family the value, placeholder and caret measurement use (a monospace token field). The field's own text layout captures the font during `render`, before any element's text style is pushed, so the family is threaded into that captured font as well as set on the box.
  - The same `font_family(name)` reaches the rest of the field family: `SearchField`, `NumberField` and `ColorField` (both its editable and static paths) forward it to the composed `Input` (NumberField also sets it on the group, so custom stepper content inherits it), `ComboBox` forwards it to its `Input` and sets it on the root for the `ComboBox.Value` line, and `Select` / `Autocomplete` set it on the trigger (Autocomplete also on the popover's filter field). Detached popover rows keep `row_font_family`. HeroGPUI extensions; v3 sets the family with a class.
  - `radius(px)` — replaces the box's corner radius. Not a v3 prop; it is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the box and shared field chrome use the same resolved radius. A bare or grouped box retains it without painting its own chrome.
  - The same `height(px)`, `padding_x(px)` and `is_bare(bool)` builders now reach the rest of the single-line family: `SearchField`, `NumberField`, `TimeField`, `DateField` and `ColorField` (both its static display box and the editable path, which forwards them to the inner `Input`). Each defaults to the stock 36px box, `px-3` inset and full chrome; a bare field keeps its geometry, editing and focus, and drops only the paint.
- **TextField** — the labelled wrapper around `Input`; forwards `start_content`, `height`, `padding_x`, `is_bare`, `focus_ring`, `font_family`, `text_size`, `radius`, `aria_label(text)` and `recipe` `aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
- **TextArea** — genuinely multi-line: one wrapping paragraph per newline, Enter inserts a newline, and the caret sits in the line it belongs to. Platform composition and paste use the shared Input handler; Enter confirms active composition before inserting a newline. Label/helper/error typography follows the shared Input wrapper (14px/20px labels; 12px/16px helper and error text). gpui wraps text by default (`WhiteSpace::Normal`); it is the single-line field that opts out with `whitespace_nowrap`. `rows`, `variant`, `full_width`, `max_length`, `min_length`, the validation flags, `on_change`, `aria_label(text)`, plus `padding_x`, `is_bare`, `focus_ring`, `font_family` and `height(px)` — a pixel floor in place of the rows-derived minimum (`rows_height = max(rows * 20px + 16px, 38px)`, HeroUI's 38px minimum), with longer content still growing the box) `aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
- **SearchField** — Input with a magnifier and clear action; labels use 14px/20px and helper/error text uses 12px/16px via the shared Input wrapper. `recipe("name")`, `text_size(px)`, `radius(px)`, `on_clear`, `is_required`, `is_read_only`, `is_invalid`
- **NumberField** — `format_options(NumberFormat)`, `NumberState {value,min,max,step,input}`, `hide_steppers`, `on_change(&f64)` `group_hover_bg(color)` is the fill the hovered group fades to over its 150ms chrome ramp, in place of `--field-hover` (`--default-hover` on the secondary variant); a focused, invalid, disabled or bare group does not hover, so the override never reaches those states (a HeroGPUI extension; v3 tints the group with a class).
  - Group text and text slots use 14px text with a 20px line height, independent of parent leading.
- **InputOTP** — `OtpState::with_length(cx, n)`, `separator`, `slot_hover_bg(color)`, `radius(px)`, `aria_label(text)`, `on_complete(&str)`. Slots carry the theme field border, variant hover fill/border, active/filled focus background, invalid danger outline, and an absolutely positioned fake caret; filled digits use the portable 250ms opacity portion of HeroUI's entrance motion. Custom slot content inherits 14px/20px text; the built-in digits use 18px/24px text. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and every slot in the row takes it in place of the field radius; the caret and the group separator keep their own smaller radius. GPUI 0.3.11 has no public scale/translate builder for the remaining character entrance transform.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
- **InputGroup** — `id()`, `variant`, `label`, `description`, `error_message` + children; `InputAddon::new("$")`. A named group reports `role="group"`. Prefix and suffix text uses 14px text with 20px lines alongside the input. `height(px)` replaces the 36px single-line group box and follows through to the held field (a textarea group stays content-sized), `padding_x(px)` replaces the held field's `px-3` on sides without an addon, `font_family(name)` threads a family through to the held field's shaping and caret measurement, `radius(px)` supplies the group shell's corner radius while the transparent held input stays `rounded-none`, and `is_bare(true)` drops the group's background, border, shadow, focus ring and hover fill while keeping the field editable. Focus-within and invalid states use the pinned field-focus fill; hover uses the 150ms ease-smooth fill transition, and prefix/suffix slots own their field-border seams. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop. `group_hover_bg(color)` is the fill the hovered group box fades to, in place of `--field-hover` (`--default-hover` on the secondary variant); a focused-within, invalid, disabled or bare group does not hover (a HeroGPUI extension; v3 tints the group with a class).
- **Checkbox** — `is_selected`, `is_indeterminate`, `hover_bg(color)`, `size(CheckboxSize::{Sm,Md})`, `radius(px)`, `is_disabled`, `is_read_only`, `is_required`, `is_invalid`, `variant(FieldVariant)`, `label(el)`, `aria_label(text)`, `on_change(&bool)`. `size` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` is the pinned 16px control / 12px indicator / 14px label; `Sm` is a 14px control with a 10px indicator and 12px label text. Label content uses medium text with 14px/20px metrics at Md and 12px/16px at Sm, independent of surrounding line height. Descriptions and errors stay aligned under the label: 28px inset at Md, 26px at Sm. Toggling animates: the accent fill scales and fades in while the check stroke draws (fill 100/200ms, draw 150ms after 15ms, undraw 200ms), a mid-flight reversal resumes from the rendered frame, and reduced motion snaps. A caller-drawn `indicator` replaces the stroke but keeps the fill motion. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: it replaces the control's default `rounded-md` only, so `is_round` keeps its documented circle either way, and the control's animated fill layers follow the resolved value. `text_size(px)` replaces the label's size-step text (a 12/14/16px size takes v3's 16/20/24 leading and any other keeps 20px); the control box, mark and description keep the step (a HeroGPUI extension).A plain-string `label("…")` names a Checkbox or Switch on its own; a composed label element needs `aria_label`.
- **CheckboxGroup** — `CheckboxGroup::new(id, options).label().value(keys).orientation().variant().is_read_only().error_message().on_change(HashSet)`, `CheckboxOption::new(key,label).description()`. Option labels use 14px/20px medium text; descriptions use 12px/16px regular text.
- **RadioGroup** — `RadioGroup::new(id, options).value().default_value().orientation().size(RadioSize::{Sm,Md}).radius(px).full_width(bool).on_change(&SharedString)`. `size` is additive, not a v3 prop: `Md` is the pinned 16px control / 6px dot / 14px label; `Sm` is 14/5/12 with a 10px row gap. Option content uses medium text with 14px/20px metrics at Md and 12px/16px at Sm, independent of surrounding line height. Descriptions and errors stay aligned under the label: 28px inset at Md, 24px at Sm. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: it rounds the control circle — the filled square v3 draws instead of a disc — in place of `key_radius`, its pressed box scales the same value, and the selected dot inside is an inner part that keeps its own. `text_size(px)` replaces the option labels' size-step text (a 12/14/16px size takes v3's 16/20/24 leading and any other keeps 20px); the circles, dot, gap and descriptions keep the step (a HeroGPUI extension).
- **Form** — `Form::new().field(FormField::text(state).is_required(true)).on_submit(&FormData).on_invalid(&FormData).on_reset()`, plus `submit_handler()` / `reset_handler()` to wire to buttons. v3's `name` rides on the field: the entity-backed ones (`Input`, `TextField`, `SearchField`, `TextArea`, `NumberField`) store it on their state and `FormField::text`/`number` read it back; the prop-based ones (`Checkbox`, `Switch`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup`, `Select`, `Slider`, `ColorSlider`, `ColorField`, `InputOTP`, `Autocomplete`, `DatePicker`, `TimeField`) expose `form_field()`, which borrows, so the control is still yours to place. `DateRangePicker` has `start_name`/`end_name` and `form_fields()`. `validationBehavior` travels the same way: `Allow` shows a field's message without blocking submission. Under the default `Native`, `validate` and constraint errors paint only after the user commits the field (change + blur; Enter or a step in NumberField/ColorField; a toggle in Checkbox/Switch; a calendar pick in DatePicker, a completed range in DateRangePicker) or submits the form, as React Stately's `useFormValidationState` does; controlled `is_invalid` and server errors stay live, and a submit still blocks on the live result. `FormData::text(name)` reads a submission. The HTTP half — `action`/`method`/`encType`/`target` — has no browser to post to.
- **Label / Description / ErrorMessage / FieldError / Fieldset** — the composition slots; `Label::new(t).is_required().is_disabled().is_invalid()`, `FieldError::new().message(t).id(id)` (stable ids enable the pinned height/opacity transition), `Fieldset::new().id()` + `FieldsetLegend` / `FieldGroup` / `FieldsetActions`. A named fieldset reports `role="group"`.

### Layout
- **Card** — `variant(CardVariant::{Transparent,Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`, `w`, `radius(px)`, parts `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`.
