The card itself is the padded box (`gap-3 p-4` and the capped container radius) and its parts carry none of their own: the header is a plain column, the title is `text-sm` medium on the foreground, the description `text-sm` muted, the content a `gap-1` column — its upstream `flex-1` is dropped, because the pinned-geometry test in `tests/card_deep.rs` measures the card as an auto-height column hugging its parts, which flex-1 regresses — and the footer a centered row. `transparent` paints nothing: no border, background or shadow. v3's Card is presentational: `isPressable`/`isHoverable`/`isBlurred` were v2, and an interactive card composes a `Button`.
- **Separator** — `id()`, `orientation`, `variant(SeparatorVariant::{Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`, `mx`/`my`. It is childless, like v3's: place separators between blocks rather than inside one (the content mode was removed in 0.11.0). The weight is `--border-width`; v3 has no per-instance override. AccessKit 0.24 has no separator role, so a named instance still produces no node.
- **Surface** — `variant(SurfaceVariant::{Transparent,Default,Secondary,Tertiary})`. The v3 component is a strict root — `relative text-foreground` plus each variant's background and foreground pair — with zero default padding and gap, and no radius or border; `transparent` is just a transparent background (the outlined look in the docs examples comes from their own `className`). `padding`/`gap` are port conveniences, not v3 props: they stand in for the `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-3xl p-6` skeleton every docs example adds through `className`. v3 also publishes its variant through `SurfaceContext` so children can read it; GPUI has no ancestor context propagation, so nothing downstream reads the surrounding surface here.
- **Toolbar** — `orientation`, `is_attached`, `gap`, `full_width(bool)`, `separator()`. Set the orientation before appending a separator; the bar creates a centred divider half its cross size.

### Media
- **Avatar** — `Avatar::new(id).name().src(ImageSource).custom_source_key(key).size().radius(px).color().variant(AvatarVariant::{Default,Soft})`, plus `on_error(f)` / `on_load(f)` for `Avatar.Image.onError`/`onLoad` (fired once per instance, no event payload), `delay_ms(ms)` for `Avatar.Fallback.delayMs` (measured from mount), `fallback(el)` for `Avatar.Fallback` children (an icon, a `+N` counter, custom text) and `fallback_color(Color)` for `Avatar.Fallback.color` — its own documented prop that overrides the parent color for everything the fallback paints. The constructor id is not a v3 prop: the image lifecycle (delay window and once-only callbacks) is keyed per instance under it, and it is required at construction so repeated avatars cannot silently merge into one instance. A changed source resets that lifecycle, so callbacks refire for the new source; a gpui `ImageSource::Custom` loader has no value identity, so omitting `custom_source_key` keeps its lifecycle stable when the closure is rebuilt inline per frame. Set `custom_source_key(key)` to identify a changed logical custom image and reset its load/error latches without using closure pointer identity. `Avatar::initials(name)` renders the default two-letter initials. Fallback text uses 12px/16px for small, 14px/20px for medium and 16px/24px for large avatars. A decoded image with zero natural size counts as a load failure (Radix Avatar 1.2.6): the fallback shows and `on_error` fires once. A plain string `src` loads through gpui's asset system; a gpui `ImageSource::Custom` loader is the custom-image-component seam. Loaded images and fallback fills share the resolved radius and explicit pixel `sx` corners of the Avatar root. Each specified corner overrides `radius`; unspecified corners keep the named or size default. Groups use `AvatarGroup`.
- **AvatarGroup** — `AvatarGroup::new(id).size().color().variant(AvatarVariant).max(n).is_grid(bool).overlap(AvatarGroupOverlap::{Clip,Ring}).overlap_distance(px).seam(px).child(Avatar).children(avatars).child_element(el).count(AvatarGroupCount).sx(..)`, `AvatarGroupCount::new(id).size().color().variant().child(el)`. The group fills `size` (default `Md`), `color` and `variant` only on direct `Avatar` children that omit them (a child's own prop wins; avatars nested in a `child_element` never inherit). `max` keeps the first `max` children and appends an automatic `+N` count; an explicit `count` is never truncated and suppresses the automatic one. `is_grid(true)` wraps with a 12px gap and no overlap; otherwise stacked siblings pull 8px under their predecessor. `Ring` is a 2px `--background` ring on every stacked child. `Clip` (the default) is a platform limitation: v3 cuts a transparent crescent with a CSS alpha mask that pinned GPUI cannot draw, so the port paints the 2px seam in `--background` — identical on a solid background, a solid seam over images or gradients. `overlap_distance` and `seam` are repository extensions for the two CSS variables. No implicit role.

### Navigation
- **Accordion** — `Accordion::new(items).expanded_keys(HashSet).variant(AccordionVariant::{Default,Surface}).radius(px).hover_bg(color).hide_separator().on_toggle(&SharedString)`, `AccordionItem::new(key,title).subtitle().content(el)`; title, subtitle and body line heights are 20px, 16px and 20px independently of host leading, with no extra top inset above the body. The built-in indicator is one down-chevron that rotates through 180 degrees over the pinned 250ms default transition curve and snaps when reduced motion is enabled; the panel measures natural body height and animates height plus opacity over the pinned 200ms curves, retaining closing content through the exit lifetime. Custom indicator content receives live `AccordionItemState` and remains caller-owned. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: it rounds the `Surface` item card in place of the container radius, so it is inert on the flush `Default` variant, which paints no card, and the separators' hairline mark keeps its own.
- **Breadcrumbs** — `Breadcrumbs::new(vec![Crumb::new("Home").href("#")]).id().separator(BreadcrumbSeparator::{Slash,Chevron,Dash}).separator_render(|i| custom node).text_size(px).full_width(bool).is_disabled(bool).on_navigate(|i, crumb, ev|)`; the last crumb is the current page — link-coloured, inert, no tab stop — even if it carries an `href`, and its AccessKit `aria-current="page"` state is exposed. Every link crumb is a tab stop and Enter/Space activates it. `text_size(px)` scales the crumb labels off their 14px default and the paired line height follows; unset keeps the fixed 14px/20px pair, and the separator keeps its own 12px. Items sit 6px apart and each item gaps its unpadded link and separator by 4px.
- **Disclosure / DisclosureGroup** — `Disclosure::new(id,title).is_expanded().on_expanded_change(&bool).content(|state: DisclosureRenderState| ..)`, `DisclosureGroup::new(id).item(key,title,content).expanded_keys().on_expanded_change()`. The built-in Disclosure indicator keeps one down-chevron and rotates it through 180 degrees over the pinned 250ms default transition curve, with the same keyed reversal and reduced-motion endpoint behavior as Accordion. Its panel measures natural body height, animates height and opacity over 200ms, and remains mounted until the close transition completes; reduced motion snaps and removes it immediately.
- **Link** — `Link::new(id).label().href().icon(el).icon_first(bool).auto_focus().radius(px).is_disabled().on_press()` plus `render(|state| el)` — v3's render function receives the link's interactive state (`isHovered`/`isPressed`/`isFocused`/`isFocusVisible`/`isDisabled`); the root keeps the `href`, `onPress`, focus and disabled wiring, and GPUI has no DOM props to spread. `.link` is `font-medium text-link no-underline decoration-[1.5px]` — the stylesheet is the contract, not the docs' `font-semibold` Global CSS snippet — and hover/press only recolour the decoration (`muted/50` → `muted`), never the text. Opening goes through the OS handler, so v3's `target` / `rel` / `download` have no meaning and are not offered. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: it replaces the root's default `rounded-xl`, which only shows against a caller-supplied background or the focus ring, since the link paints no fill of its own.
- **Pagination** — `Pagination::new(id, page, total).size().full_width(bool).hover_bg(color).on_change(&usize)` — the active page exposes AccessKit `aria-current="page"`; the override feeds hover and pressed together; summary, link and navigation text use size-specific 12/16, 14/20 and 16/24 font/line-height pairs independently of host leading.
- **Tabs** — `Tabs::new(id, items, selected_key).variant(TabsVariant::{Primary,Secondary}).align(TabsAlign::{Start,Center,End}).orientation().size(TabsSize::{Sm,Md}).full_width(bool).selected_key().default_selected_key().on_selection_change()`, `TabItem::new(key,label).content(el)`; `full_width(true)` is v3's `<Tabs.List className="w-full">` with `<Tabs.Trigger className="flex-1">` — the horizontal list fills its parent and the tabs take equal shares of it instead of hugging their labels (ignored when vertical, where tabs already stretch); `align` positions content inside each tab, defaulting to Center, without changing selection, indicator geometry, panel content, or nested lists; Start and End follow the left-to-right layout. Labels use a released `min_w(0)` slot with normal whitespace when a tab share is constrained; vertical lists release only their cross-axis min-content floor beside the panel, keep their scroll column intrinsic on the main axis, and the tab keeps the pinned fixed 32px box in both variants: the stylesheet has no truncate or overflow utility on the tab, so a wrapped label's overflow lines paint past the pill the way the default overflow does instead of growing the box (they stay pointer-inert, while browser hit testing follows painted text). Both tab variants use 14px labels with a 20px line height independently of host leading. `size(Sm)` is a 28px box with 12px padding and a 12px label on a 16px leading; the default `Md` is byte-identical to the pinned box. `vertical_tab_min_width(px)` replaces the 80px floor (`min-w-20`) every tab of a vertical list keeps; a horizontal list ignores it and `TabItem::width` still wins (a HeroGPUI extension). `text_size(px)` replaces the tab labels' size-step text (a 12/14/16px size takes v3's 16/20/24 leading and any other keeps 20px); each tab keeps its fixed height and padding, so a larger type wants `TabItem::height` (a HeroGPUI extension).
  - Wheel input scrolls the tab list only along its configured orientation.
  - Icon-only segmented control: `TabItem::trigger(el)` renders the element as the segment's own trigger in place of the label text — the tab keeps its id, hit area, hover, focus ring and keyboard activation, and `label` stays the accessible name (an icon child carries none; the trigger is presentational, so keep it a plain `svg()` or `div()` and set the svg's `text_color` explicitly). `radius(px)` gives the list container and the indicator one exact corner in place of the derived container radius and the `control_radius` pill (tab boxes, their hover fades and focus rings keep the pinned radius); `list_bg(color)` overrides the tray fill (`bg-default` primary, transparent secondary); `indicator_bg(color)` overrides the indicator fill in both variants, including the pre-measurement active-tab fallback that paints the same look before geometry arrives; `indicator_shadow(false)` drops the indicator's `shadow-surface` and its fallback. All four refine the resolved theme values and leave the pinned rendering untouched when unused — together they build the reference capture toolbar's `rounded-3xl` tray and pill with muted fills and no shadow. Fixed boxes name the toolbar's `size-8 p-0` segment the same way: `TabItem::width(px)` fixes the segment's width over the content-hugging box in both variants — it also wins over `full_width`'s equal share for that tab alone (its siblings still divide what is left) and replaces the vertical list's 80px minimum — `TabItem::height(px)` replaces the size step's tab height (still a fixed box, so wrapped lines keep painting past it), and `TabItem::padding_x(px)` replaces the step's horizontal padding, `0` meaning none; the sliding indicator measures the fixed box, so its geometry, entry motion and re-targeting follow the override exactly. `Tabs::list_padding(px)` overrides the primary tray's uniform inset — `Tabs.List className="p-0"` is `list_padding(0)`; the Secondary tray has no inset of its own (v3's secondary block already replaces the list's `p-1` with `p-0`), so the builder is Primary-only. `Tabs::hover_fill(false)` stops painting the unselected-tab hover wash — the tray-dimmed overlay the port paints for the stylesheet's `opacity-70` dim, resolved from the same tray fill `list_bg` and a root `sx` background produce — and instead recolours a hovered unselected label to the theme foreground, leaving the resting fill, the selected fill, the indicator and the focus rings untouched, while the overflow chevrons keep their own dim; the default keeps the wash. A `trigger` svg still needs its own `text_color` (gpui svgs do not inherit the tab's), so this hover cannot recolour an icon the caller painted explicitly. With `width(32).height(32).padding_x(0)`, `list_padding(0)` and `hover_fill(false)` the segments tile the tray edge to edge exactly as the reference toolbar's does.

### Overlays

Modal, Drawer, and AlertDialog cover the window even inside clipped or positioned containers. They paint above later page content and block pointer input to the page beneath.

- **AlertDialog** — `AlertDialog::new(title).id().description().is_open().size(AlertDialogSize::{Xs,Sm,Md,Lg,Cover}).backdrop(Backdrop).placement(ModalPlacement).status(Color).radius(px).is_dismissible(bool).is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled(bool).confirm_label().cancel_label().on_confirm().on_cancel().on_open_change(&bool)` plus composed children; `.child(AlertDialogCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `AlertDialog.CloseTrigger` X and `.footer_child(Button)` composes the caller-owned footer. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop: it replaces the panel's default container radius, the entry zoom interpolates the same value, and the status icon's `rounded-3xl` tile is an inner part that keeps its own.
  The description wraps inside the body; overflowing body content scrolls within the panel.
  - every close path — the composed X, the backdrop and Escape — reports through `on_open_change(false)` first; the built-in confirm/cancel stand-in reports through it too, then fires the consumer action. Escape and the backdrop are plain closes and never call `on_cancel`.
  - a composed footer retires the built-in pair: the caller's own `Button`s own their close wiring and the danger/pending spellings (`variant(Variant::Danger)`, `is_pending(true)`), the way v3 composes `slot="close"` buttons.
  - `is_dismissible` and `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled` default to v3's values (backdrop dismissal off, Escape off), so opting in is explicit. `status` renders the alert glyph in that role's colour and only when set.
  - placement is anchored like Modal's, but v3's ±4px enter slide for top/bottom/auto is not ported — the fade and the zoom are.
- **Drawer** — `placement(DrawerPlacement)`, `size(px)`, `title`, `backdrop(Backdrop)`, `is_dismissible`, `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`, `footer_child`, `on_close(&DismissReason)`, `on_open_change(&bool)`; `.child(DrawerCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `Drawer.CloseTrigger` X and `.child(DrawerHandle::new())` composes v3's optional `Drawer.Handle` drag bar — rendered only where composed: before the header on every placement except Top, where it follows the footer at the moving edge, and it keeps the drag-to-dismiss wiring only while `is_dismissible`
- **Modal** — `is_open`, `title`, `size(ModalSize::{Xs,Sm,Md,Lg,Cover,Full})`, `backdrop(Backdrop)`, `placement(ModalPlacement::{Auto,Center,Top,Bottom})`, `scroll(ModalScroll::{Inside,Outside})`, `radius(px)`, `panel_width(px)`, `padding(px)`, `is_dismissible`, `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`, `footer_child`, `on_close(&DismissReason)`, `on_open_change(&bool)`; `.child(ModalCloseTrigger::new())` composes v3's `Modal.CloseTrigger` X — the part draws only where composed, like v3
  - `Inside` scrolling retains a 40px outer margin, including with long content; `Full` fills the viewport. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`; it replaces the default panel radius but `Full` paints no radius either way, so its zoom stays a plain fade.
  - every dismissal path reports through **both** `on_close` and `on_open_change(false)`, so either callback alone is sufficient. `on_close` receives a `#[non_exhaustive]` `DismissReason` — `CloseButton`, `Escape`, `Backdrop`, or (Drawer) `Drag` — naming the path that fired.
  - Escape closes it unless `is_keyboard_dismiss_disabled`. The overlay takes a focus handle and claims focus while nothing inside holds it; keys bubble from the focused descendant, so a text field inside keeps working. Drawer and AlertDialog behave the same way (AlertDialog defaults keyboard dismissal *off*, as v3 does).
Pressable Button, ToggleButton and CloseButton roots expose the `Button` keyboard context. An open Popover exposes `Popover`; application shortcut predicates can exclude these contexts when native control activation should own the key.

- **Popover** — `Popover::new(trigger).is_open().placement(Placement).offset(px).should_flip(bool).padding(px).radius(px).panel_width(px).aria_label(label).title().show_close_button().on_open_change(&bool)`; `panel_width` replaces the 260px resting width and its entry/exit geometry; `aria_label` names a panel without adding a visible heading. Modal `panel_width` overrides its width preset and `padding` overrides its 24px inset, with viewport containment preserved. These are repository extensions; defaults remain unchanged. Panel text defaults to 14px with a 20px line height independently of host leading; `.child(PopoverArrow::new())` composes v3's `Popover.Arrow` part — the built-in 12px curve, or a custom child element at the resolved position but without the rotation (upstream rotates it through its `data-slot` placement CSS; The pinned GPUI transforms only `svg()` elements at construction). `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the panel's entry zoom interpolates the override, so the animation never parts company with the painted shape.
  - `should_flip` routes through gpui's `anchored().snap_to_window()`, which slides the panel back inside the viewport rather than mirroring it to the opposite side.
- **Sheet** — `Sheet::new(id)` is a modal edge overlay; `trigger(Button)` opens its uncontrolled state, `default_open(bool)` seeds it, and `is_open(bool)` with `on_open_change` makes it controlled. `placement(DrawerPlacement::{Bottom,Top,Left,Right})`, `is_detached(bool)`, `backdrop(Backdrop)`, `snap_points([160., 320.])`, `title`, `aria_label`, `role(a11y::Role::{Dialog,AlertDialog})`, `sx` (refines the panel).
  - `snap_points` numbers are pixels; `SheetSnapPoint::Fraction(0.5)` is a percentage of the full panel. Full expansion is implicit, a trailing pixel `1` or fraction `1.0` is ignored, and arbitrary CSS lengths are not parsed.
  - body `child`/`children`, `footer_child`, `close_child(Button)` (runs the action and closes), `close_trigger(CloseButton)` (preserves its action and disabling), `handle(element)`, `content(|SheetState| element)` (`is_expanded`, visible pixel `position`), and `nested_child(Sheet)`.
  - `is_dismissible(false)` blocks Escape, outside presses and swipe dismissal; explicit close controls work. The mouse handle expands and snaps; the body scrolls at full expansion. Browser touch scroll gestures and the covered parent's 3D scaling are not available. Only the outer sheet dims the page. Closing returns focus and removes caller content immediately; the measured panel chrome completes its exit without live controls. Fractional snap points and full expansion follow viewport resizing. The topmost sheet owns dismissal.
  - `on_close` receives `DismissReason`; `on_animation_end(&bool)` reports an uninterrupted 500ms enter or exit (immediate with reduced motion). Retained closed content (`isExiting`) is not ported because GPUI has no inert painted subtree.
- **Toast** — `Toast::new(title).description().variant(Color).indicator(Option<SharedString>).indicator_content(|cx| element).closable().close_hover_bg(color).padding(px).radius(px).push(duration, cx)`; `indicator_content` renders fresh caller-owned GPUI content inside the pinned 24px indicator box while `indicator(None)` suppresses it. `Toast::new(title).variant(Color).timeout(duration).update(id, cx)` is `toast.update` and keeps the card’s stack position, inheriting an omitted timeout/`onClose`; a missing id falls back to a new toast. `Toast::promise(future, loading, cx)` is `toast.promise`: a loading toast updates in place to the success or danger variant when the future settles, then the default dismiss clock starts. The GPUI lifecycle extension `Toast::promise_task(future, loading, cx)` returns `(id, Task<()>)`; retain or detach the task to allow completion. Dropping it cancels pending work and leaves the loading toast for the owner to dismiss or clear. `ToastViewport::new().id().placement(ToastPlacement).gap().max_visible_toasts().width().is_expanded(bool).exit_duration(Duration).hotkey(ToastHotkey)` is `Toast.Provider` and a named viewport reports `role="region"`; `toast_store(cx)` global. The stack expands on hover, focus-within, or `is_expanded(true)` when more than one toast is active; interaction pause stops the clocks, but a forced expand does not. Overflow past `maxVisibleToasts` stays queued as hidden cards. Dismissed cards stay mounted for `exitDuration` (300ms) unless reduced motion is on. Toast titles wrap naturally, and the close affordance is absolutely anchored at the card’s top/end edge so it does not steal message width. The default hotkey is Alt+T. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, and the card’s entry zoom interpolates the override, so the animation never parts company with the painted shape; the close button inside the card keeps its own smaller radius.
- **Tooltip** — `Tooltip::new("tip").placement(TooltipPlacement)` takes the shared 22-value placement vocabulary (`Placement` aliased, so the same variants as Popover: `Top`…`EndBottom`). `show_arrow(bool).offset(px).radius(px).delay(ms).close_delay(ms).is_disabled().child(trigger)`. `body(|window, cx| element)` draws the tip's body yourself — a small table, a key/value list, a legend — in place of the measured single line; the string handed to `Tooltip::new` is still required and remains the tip's accessible name and default hover key, so a rich tip cannot ship unnamed. The string path reconstructs CSS `max-content` capped at 320px by shaping the line; an element body skips that and takes its own intrinsic width under the same cap. The closure runs only while the tip is on screen. Side-plus-alignment placements align the panel and arrow to the corresponding trigger edge; logical start/end aliases land on the matching physical side's pixels because the port is LTR-only.
  - stateful: hover state lives in a per-tooltip `Window::use_keyed_state` entity, so `delay` / `closeDelay` work without the caller threading an entity through. Defaults come from the `--tooltip-delay` / `--tooltip-close-delay` theme tokens.
  - a generation counter invalidates a timer whose hover has already been superseded, which is what stops a fast pass across a row of triggers from opening all of them.
  - the key defaults to the tip text; give two tooltips with the same text distinct `id`s.

### Pickers
- **Autocomplete** — `Autocomplete::new(state, items).placement(Placement).max_items().radius(px).on_selection_change()` — filters while focused. Items are `PickerItem::new(key, label)`: v3 keeps a stable `Key` separate from the visible `textValue`, so `value` / `defaultValue` / `disabledKeys`, the selection callbacks and the form value address items by key, while filtering and the trigger's visible text use labels — duplicate labels never alias each other's selection or row. Value, option and empty-result text uses 14px/20px metrics; selected and placeholder values wrap at word boundaries inside the trigger, natural and virtual option rows keep normal text flow, and the selected/custom marker sits in an absolute 16px trailing slot with 28px reserved end padding. The clear affordance keeps its 20px target, scales its visual to .93 while pressed, hides immediately when empty and eases in over 150ms when a selection reappears; reduced motion snaps that visual. A fixed virtual row height remains caller-owned geometry. Section headers use 12px/16px medium text. The popup anchors to the measured trigger with an 8px gap, flipping to the side with more room when the preferred side cannot fit and keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; the search stays visible while the inner list scrolls and shrinks to the available height within the upstream 320px max, and virtual paging follows the visible list height. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius. When the caller removes the highlighted item, the highlight moves to the next enabled match, or the previous one when none follows.
  - `filter(fn(item_label, input) -> bool)` replaces the default case-insensitive substring match and owns the whole decision, including what an empty query means; `input_value` / `on_input_change` for a controlled query; `on_clear` is only the after-clear callback — the clear affordance is always mounted with the trigger, invisible and inert while the selection is empty or the field is disabled, and still working when read-only.
- **ComboBox** — `ComboBox::new(state, items).is_open().placement(Placement).menu_trigger(MenuTrigger::{Input,Manual,Focus}).allows_custom_value().max_items().radius(px).on_selection_change().on_open_change()` — items are keyed `PickerItem::new(key, label)`s: the selection, `disabledKeys`, the callbacks and the form value address items by key, while filtering and the input text use labels. `selected_keys(keys)` is the controlled ordered selection; `selected_key(key)` the single-key spelling (the empty string is v3's `null`). `on_selection_change_all` reports one key for a changed single pick by pointer, Enter or Tab, and the whole ordered set in multiple mode. Re-picking the current single key leaves this value callback silent; `on_selection_change` retains its pick notification. Controlled changes remain requests until the caller accepts them. Read-only fields reject row picks even when their popover is already open. A committed custom value keeps the typed text and reports a null selected key — as an empty `on_selection_change_all` slice, and only when a selection actually existed; `form_value(ComboBoxFormValue::{Key,Text})` chooses what a named field submits (key by default — an empty selection still submits one empty value — and text under `allowsCustomValue`). Value, option and empty-result text uses 14px/20px metrics; the optional `ComboBox.Value` default content and natural and virtual option rows keep normal text flow, while custom renderers retain child ownership; selected markers use an absolute 16px trailing slot with 28px reserved end padding. A fixed virtual row height remains caller-owned geometry. Section headers use 12px/16px medium text. The built-in trigger chevron rotates over 150ms, and a closed popup remains mounted for the pinned 100ms fade/zoom exit without intercepting the next pointer target. When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; plain and virtual lists use the available height with an 8px field gap, and wheel input stays in the list. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger is the inner `Input`'s box and keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius. `min_width(px)` replaces the 180px floor the root keeps while not `full_width` (a full-width combo box has none either way); a HeroGPUI extension, v3 sizes the root with a class. Opening highlights the selected item when it is an enabled match for the current query; otherwise ArrowDown and ArrowUp open onto the row their move lands on, a keyboard press of the button onto the first match, and a pointer press or a typed query highlights nothing. When the caller removes the highlighted item (with the query unchanged), the highlight moves to the next enabled match, or the previous one when none follows.
- **Select** — `Select::new(id, options).value(..).is_open().placement(Placement).variant().full_width().disabled_keys().is_invalid().is_required().radius(px).recipe("name").aria_label(text).on_selection_change()/.on_change().on_open_change()` (`recipe` stacks `Theme.components.select` recipes); `selection_mode(SelectionMode::Multiple)` with `selected_keys()` + `on_selection_change_all()`. `item_leading(|key, is_selected| Option<AnyElement>)` draws a per-row leading element before each option's label — v3's `ListBox.Item` render function, for swatch, avatar or icon rows; `PickerItem` stays a key and a label because the combo box, autocomplete, tag filter and swatch picker share it. `padding_y(px)` adds v3's `py-2` to the trigger: the trigger is a `min-h` box, so a single-line value stays exactly 36px and only a value that wraps to two lines grows, which is the case a fixed `height` cannot express. `trigger_indicator(|is_open| ..)` replaces the trigger chevron and receives the live open state; the built-in SVG rotates over the pinned 150ms transition. `row_height(px)` is `ListLayout`'s `rowHeight` and what virtualizes the popup list through `uniform_list`: every option is exactly that tall, including the option box inside the row (it does not keep the 36px `.list-box-item` floor a plain list has). Enabled options use the shared 98% press skin with the pinned 250ms `ease-out-quart` transition inside a stable row slot. Enter and Space commit the highlighted option in single mode; if the selection callback closes the controlled popup, key release keeps it closed and leaves focus on the trigger. Value and option text uses 14px/20px metrics; long trigger values and natural and virtual option rows keep normal text flow, selected/custom markers sit in an absolute 16px trailing slot with 28px reserved end padding, and a fixed virtual row height remains caller-owned geometry; section headers use 12px/16px medium text. `full_width(true)` expands both the root and trigger to the available container width. When the preferred side cannot fit the popup, it flips to the side with more room, keeping a 12px cross-axis viewport inset with the scroller capped to the available height; plain and virtual lists use the available height with an 8px trigger gap. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it is the detached panel's corner — the panel's entry zoom interpolates the same value — while the trigger keeps the shared field chrome's own field radius. `clear_button(SelectClearButton::new().child(content).on_click(callback))` composes an optional clear control; omit `child` for the default icon. `on_clear(callback)` reports clearing after the selection callback. It clears the whole selection, including required fields; controlled owners receive the request without losing ownership. Backspace/Delete work only on a nonempty, enabled, closed trigger with a clear part composed. Empty controls retain layout space and do not intercept clicks. Opening highlights the selected option (the first enabled one in selection order); with none, Enter, Space and ArrowDown open onto the first enabled option, ArrowUp onto the last, and a pointer open highlights nothing. When the caller removes the highlighted option, the highlight moves to the next enabled option, or the previous one when none follows.`aria_label(text)` sets the accessible name explicitly, ahead of any label- or content-derived name.
  - `item_content(|key, is_selected, window, cx| AnyElement)` replaces each option’s visible content while preserving the `PickerItem` label for accessibility and typeahead; it takes precedence over `item_leading` and keeps Select’s indicator. `panel_gap(px)` and `SelectStyle::panel_gap` set inter-option spacing for natural and virtual lists; unset retains zero spacing. `panel_min_width(px)` / `SelectStyle::panel_min_width` set a minimum detached-panel width while retaining trigger-width matching.
  - Compact parts: `trigger_text_size(px(12.))`, `row_text_size(px(12.))`, `panel_padding(px(4.))`; defaults stay 14px, 14px and 6px. Panel entry/exit uses the configured padding. Only the active single/multiple selection axis owns state; a single controlled select needs only `value`, a multiple controlled select only `selected_keys`.
  - The collection box seam: `Select` and `Autocomplete` accept `height(px)`, `padding_x(px)` and `is_bare(bool)` on the trigger, and every collection (`Select`, `ComboBox`, `Autocomplete`, `ListBox`) accepts `row_padding_x(px)` / `row_padding_y(px)` for its option rows and `row_hover_bg(color)` for the fill a hovered row takes. `Select`, `ComboBox` and `Autocomplete` also accept `row_font_family(name)` for their detached popover rows, which do not inherit the trigger's font. Defaults are the stock metrics (`8/6` on ComboBox and ListBox, `10/6` on Select and Autocomplete). `Select` adds `padding_y(px)` (also `SelectStyle::padding_y`), which the rest of the family does not carry because their single-line editor never wraps. Note that `sx` on these components refines the component *root*, not the trigger, so trigger geometry has to come from these builders. An explicit `height` fixes the trigger box, so content taller than it overflows; unset keeps the 36px minimum and grows with content; `ComboBox` forwards its three trigger builders to the inner `Input`, and `is_bare` drops only the paint while the list still opens and selects. `Select::trigger_hover_bg(color)` and `Autocomplete::trigger_hover_bg(color)` name the fill a hovered trigger fades to, in place of `--field-hover` (`--default-hover` on the secondary variant); focus, invalid, disabled and bare triggers keep their own chrome, and hovering Autocomplete's clear button still suppresses the trigger hover. `Autocomplete::clear_hover_bg(color)` is that clear button's hover fill, in place of `--default-hover`.

### Typography
The browser gallery bundles distinct Inter faces for Normal, Medium, Semibold and Bold weights.
- **Kbd** — `Kbd::new().variant(KbdVariant::{Default,Light}).radius(px)` plus arbitrary children; v3's parts are `KbdAbbr::new(KbdKey)` (renders `KbdKey::symbol()`, the accessible name is `KbdKey::label()`) and `KbdContent::new()` for the key text. `KbdKey` covers all 22 v3 `keyValue`s (Command, Shift, Ctrl, Option, Enter, Delete, Escape, Tab, CapsLock, arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End, Help, Space, Fn, Win, Alt).
- **Typography** — `Typography::new(text).kind(TypographyType::{H1..H6,Body,BodySm,BodyXs,Code}).align().color(TextColor::{Default,Muted}).weight(FontWeight).font_family(name).radius(px).truncate()`; helpers `heading(level, t)`, `paragraph(ParagraphSize, t)`, `code(t)`; `Prose::new()` for rich text. `radius` is the same per-component repository extension as `Button::radius`, not the removed v2 prop, and it rounds the inline `Code` chip in place of `mark_radius` — the only kind that paints a box, so every other kind ignores it.

### Utilities
- **ScrollShadow** — `ScrollShadow::new(id).orientation().size(px).offset(px).visibility(ScrollShadowVisibility).is_enabled(bool).hide_scroll_bar(bool).max_h()/.max_w()`, `horizontal()` shorthand. v3's `variant` has one value. A painted overlay thumb uses `--scrollbar` unless `hide_scroll_bar` is set.
- **Scrollbar** — `Scrollbar::new(id, ScrollHandle).orientation(Orientation).track(px).inset(px).radius(px).thumb_color(Hsla).thumb_hover_color(Hsla).auto_hide(bool).sx(|s| ..)`. Overlay thumb painted from the `--scrollbar` token; it auto-hides when the OS preference says so, and `auto_hide(false)` pins it visible the way a styled webkit scrollbar is (true or unset keeps the stock behavior). `track` sizes the gutter — default 8px — `inset` shrinks the painted thumb from every edge — default 0 — and the thumb's corners default to half the effective track, so an overridden `track` (or `sx` size) re-derives them, with `radius` naming them explicitly. `thumb_color` replaces the token and `thumb_hover_color` is the fill the thumb takes while the pointer is anywhere over the bar's track — the thumb paints without a hitbox, so there is no thumb-only hover; unset, hovering changes nothing. These are repository extensions — HeroUI styles scrollbars through CSS, so there is no v3 prop to port.
  - The `sx` slot refines the track root: an `sx` background is the thumb's resting fill (it also paints the transparent gutter, so `thumb_color` is the seam that moves only the thumb), a definite cross-axis `w`/`h` is the track thickness the default radius derives from, and per-corner radii shape the thumb. Hover feedback is an immediate swap, not a transition — the thumb is painted from the handle at paint time, outside gpui's style hover system.
  - Wheel input scrolls only along the configured orientation.

## HeroGPUI extensions

Not HeroUI v3 APIs; each is labelled as an extension in its rustdoc and kept
out of `reference_metadata`.

- **Shared builder traits** — `Disableable::is_disabled(bool)`,
  `Sizable::size(Self::Size)` and `Selectable::is_selected(bool)`, for generic
  code over components (`fn f<T: Disableable + Sizable<Size = Size>>(t: T)`).
  Every impl delegates to the inherent builder of the same name, which stays
  the documented API. `Sizable::Size` is the component's own scale (`Size`,
  `ModalSize`, `CheckboxSize`, `SpinnerSize`, ...).
- **i18n** — `i18n::set_locale("de-DE", cx)`, `i18n::locale(cx)`,
  `i18n::ui_string(UiString::Close, cx)`, `i18n::ui_string_with(UiString::Increase,
  "Quantity", cx)` (fills a template's one `{..}` placeholder; `i18n::fill`),
  `i18n::set_ui_string("fr", UiString::Loading, "Chargement", cx)`,
  `i18n::lookup(locale, key)`. `UiString` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, `ALL`,
  `COUNT`): `SelectPlaceholder`, `NoResults`, `Close`, `Loading`,
  `Previous`, `Next`, `Remove`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Search`, `Increase` /
  `Decrease` (NumberField and TimeField steppers, `{fieldLabel}` templates),
  `Year`, `Month`, `Day`, `Hour`, `Minute`, `Second`, `DayPeriod` (DateField
  and TimeField segment names), `Calendar` (DatePicker / DateRangePicker
  trigger), `DateSelected` (a selected calendar day, `{date}` template),
  `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Lightness`, `Brightness`, `Red`, `Green`, `Blue`,
  `Alpha` (colour channels; `ColorChannel::localized_label(cx)`, drawn by
  ColorSlider), `ClearSelection` (Autocomplete clear button), `Pagination`
  (Pagination's navigation name), `LoadingMore` (Table's pending load-more
  row, `Loading…`). Resolution: exact override, then an
  override for the bare language, then the built-in table (exact tag, then
  language), then en-US. Built-in (`LOCALES`): en-US, de-DE, es-ES, fr-FR,
  it-IT, nl-NL, pl-PL, pt-BR, sv-SE, ja-JP, zh-CN, ko-KR, ru-RU, every key
  translated — from the pinned React Aria 3.53.1 / React Stately 3.51.0 /
  RAC 1.22.1 dictionaries, except `NoResults`, `Loading`, `Search`,
  `ClearSelection` and `Pagination`, which HeroUI hard-codes in English and
  HeroGPUI translates itself. Dates and numbers keep their own per-component
  ICU4X `.locale(..)`. The web gallery bundles Noto Sans SC (hanzi, kana,
  kanji) and Noto Sans KR (Hangul) subsets for the non-Latin rows; Inter
  covers Cyrillic.
- **Theme files** (`serde` feature) — `register_theme_json(json, cx)`
  registers a `ThemeDocument` without activating it; `load_themes_dir(dir,
  cx)` does that for every `*.json` in a directory (name order);
  `presets::register_presets(cx)` adds `ocean`, `forest`, `midnight` and
  `rose`; switch with `use_theme(id, cx)`. `THEME_SCHEMA` is the JSON Schema
  (`crates/herogpui-theme/theme.schema.json`). `ThemeProvider::insert` and
  `ThemeProvider::theme_ids` are the registry primitives.
- **Theme hot reload** (`watch` feature, implies `serde`; native only) —
  `watch_themes_dir(dir, |reload: &ThemeReload, cx| .., cx) -> Result<ThemeWatcher, ThemeLoadError>`
  polls `dir` every `THEME_WATCH_INTERVAL` (500ms) on GPUI's executors and
  re-registers each `*.json` whose contents changed, plus new files; an edit
  to the active theme's file swaps its tokens in place and repaints. Files
  present at the call count as loaded (call `load_themes_dir` first). A file
  that fails to parse keeps its last good theme and appears once in
  `ThemeReload::errors`; `ThemeReload::reloaded` lists the re-registered ids.
  Dropping the `#[must_use]` `ThemeWatcher` stops the watch. Polling, not an
  OS notification crate, so the feature adds no dependency. The native
  gallery watches `HEROGPUI_THEME_DIR=<dir>` (activating its first theme).
- **Test kit** (`test-support` feature) — `herogpui::test::open_window(cx,
  |_, _| View)` returns `(Entity<View>, &mut VisualTestContext)`;
  `TestWindowExt` adds `find(selector)`, `expect(selector)`,
  `click(selector)`, `click_at(point)`, `hover`, `press("tab enter")` (with
  the key-up GPUI activates on), `type_text`, `scroll` and `settle`.
  Elements are addressed by `.debug_selector(..)`. With `use herogpui::*;`
  in a test file, add `use ::core::prelude::v1::test;` so `#[gpui::test]`
  expands to the built-in test attribute.
- **VirtualList** — `VirtualList::new(id, &handle, |ix, window, cx|
  row.into_any_element()).height(px)` over a caller-owned handle, which
  picks the mode: `VirtualListHandle::new(count)` measures rows that differ
  in height as they are built (GPUI `list`); `VirtualListHandle::uniform(count)`
  lays every row out at the first row's height (GPUI `uniform_list`), and
  without `.height(..)` sizes to its rows. `handle.scroll_to_item(ix,
  VirtualListScroll::{Reveal, Top, Center})` (`#[non_exhaustive]`; Center
  moves only a row that is not fully visible and clamps at the ends),
  `set_item_count(n)` (scrolls to the top), `splice(range, count)` (keeps the
  scroll), `remeasure()`, `scroll_by(px)`, `first_visible_item()`,
  `bounds_for_item(ix)`, `viewport_bounds()` (the laid-out viewport, for
  paging), `remaining_below()` (content below the viewport; exact in uniform
  mode, known in measured mode only once the last row was laid out),
  `is_scrolled_to_top()`, `is_scrolled_to_end()`, `is_uniform()`. In measured
  mode Reveal and Center on a row not laid out in the last frame fall back to
  Top. `ListBox` and `Table` render their `estimated_row_height` bodies in
  measured mode and their `row_height` bodies, like ComboBox's popover list,
  in uniform mode.
- **ContextMenu** — `ContextMenu::new(id, area, items).on_action(|key, w,
  cx| ..).on_open_change(..).disabled_keys([..]).is_disabled(bool)`. A
  secondary (right) press in the area opens the Dropdown `Menu` panel at the
  pointer; an item, Escape or an outside press closes it. Shift+F10 or the
  ContextMenu key (`menu`, or `contextmenu` on the web) with the focus inside
  the area opens it below the focused HeroGPUI control when that control
  records its painted bounds (including buttons, fields and active list or
  tree rows); otherwise it uses the area's top-left corner. The first item
  receives focus, and closing returns it. The area is focusable outside the
  tab order: a primary press on non-focusable content focuses it. The panel
  takes Dropdown's styling surface: `.recipe("name")` stacks
  `Theme.components.menu` recipes (row hover fill, `panel_min_width`,
  padding, radius and the rest of `MenuStyle`), and `.item_content(..)` /
  `.item_start_content(..)` forward to the `Menu` rows.
- **MenuBar** — `MenuBar::new(id, vec![MenuBarMenu::new(key, label,
  items).disabled_keys([..]).is_disabled(bool), ..]).on_action(|menu, item,
  w, cx| ..).on_open_change(|open: &Option<SharedString>, w, cx| ..)`. A
  horizontal bar of Dropdown `Menu` panels (HeroGPUI extension). One trigger
  is a tab stop; Left/Right rove between triggers (wrapping, skipping
  disabled), Home/End jump; a press, Enter, Space or Down opens (keyboard
  opens focus the first item). While open, Left/Right or hovering another
  trigger switches menus; Escape, a pick, an outside press or pressing the
  open trigger closes and refocuses its trigger. Roles: `MenuBar`, and
  `MenuItem` + expanded on each trigger.
- **ResizablePanelGroup** — `ResizablePanelGroup::new(id).orientation(
  Orientation::{Horizontal, Vertical}).panel(ResizablePanel::new()
  .default_size(pct).min_size(pct).max_size(pct).child(el)).panels([..])
  .on_resize(|sizes: &[f32], w, cx| ..).keyboard_step(pct).is_disabled(bool)`;
  `.sizes([..])` makes it controlled. Sizes are percentages of the space the
  panels share (the group minus its 8px `RESIZABLE_HANDLE_SIZE` handles) and
  sum to 100; panels without a default share the remainder. Defaults and
  controlled sizes that do not sum to 100 are scaled to it (an even split
  when they sum to zero) and moved inside the panels' min/max. A handle drag
  (pointer captured) or the arrow keys on a focused handle (Left/Right, or
  Up/Down when vertical; Shift is 4x the step; Home/End to the limits)
  resize only the two adjacent panels, clamped to their min/max. Pixel
  limits `.min_size_px(px)` / `.max_size_px(px)` combine with the percentages
  (the stricter wins) against the group's measured length, from the frame
  after the first layout, for defaults, drags, keys and window resizes.
  `.collapsible(true).collapsed_size(pct)` (default 0) lets a panel sit
  below its minimum at the collapsed size: a drag past halfway between the
  two collapses or expands it, an arrow key crosses the gap, Home/End reach
  it, and Enter on a handle collapses the panel before it (or the one after,
  when only that is collapsible) and restores its pre-collapse size.
  `.on_resize_end(|sizes, w, cx| ..)` fires once per gesture: on the release
  of a drag that changed the sizes and after each key that did. Each handle
  is a tab stop reporting `Splitter` with orientation and a value range.
- **TreeView** — `TreeView::new(id, vec![TreeItem::new(key, label)
  .children([..]).icon(path).is_disabled(bool), ..]).selection_mode(
  SelectionMode::{None, Single, Multiple})` (default `None`),
  `.selected_keys([..])` / `.default_selected_keys([..])`,
  `.expanded_keys([..])` / `.default_expanded_keys([..])`,
  `.disabled_keys([..])`, `.disallow_empty_selection(bool)`,
  `.is_disabled(bool)`, `.max_h(px)`, `.on_selection_change(|&HashSet<SharedString>, w,
  cx| ..)`, `.on_expanded_change(..)`. One tab stop; Up/Down/Home/End over
  visible rows (skipping disabled), Right expands then enters the first
  child, Left collapses then goes to the parent, typeahead; the chevron
  toggles a parent; a press, Enter or Space toggles selection (with mode
  `None`, toggles a parent's expansion); Escape clears the selection. In
  `Multiple`, Shift+Up/Down and a Shift press extend the selection from
  the anchor (the last row a press or Space selected) over the visible,
  enabled rows between; Shift+Home/End only move. Rows render through a
  uniform `VirtualList`: under `max_h` (or a height-bounding parent) only
  the rows in view are built and the cursor scrolls into view. Roles:
  `Tree`, `TreeItem` with level, `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize` among its
  siblings, expanded and selected.
- **Icons** — `Icon::new(IconName::Search).size(px(20.)).color(hsla)`
  draws an embedded Lucide icon (default 16px, `DEFAULT_ICON_SIZE`, in the
  theme `foreground`; gpui svgs do not inherit text colour). `size` also
  takes an `IconSize` step (`Xs` 12, `Sm` 14, `Md` 16, `Lg` 20, `Xl` 24px;
  `Icon` implements `Sizable<Size = IconSize>`). `.stroke_width(w)` is
  Lucide's `strokeWidth` in the 24-unit viewBox (default
  `DEFAULT_STROKE_WIDTH`, 2) and `.absolute_stroke_width(true)` its
  `absoluteStrokeWidth` (`w * 24 / size`, so the stroke stays `w` pixels);
  it draws `IconName::path_with_stroke_width(w)`
  (`<path>?stroke-width=<w>`), which `HeroGpuiAssets` serves as the same
  file with its root `stroke-width` rewritten (Lucide icons only; an app
  serving Lucide paths itself must forward the query);
  `Icon::from_path(icons::CHECK)` draws any other served SVG. `IconName` is
  a curated, `#[non_exhaustive]` subset of Lucide `LUCIDE_VERSION` (1.31.0),
  one PascalCase variant per Lucide name (`circle-check` is
  `IconName::CircleCheck`): `IconName::ALL`, `.name()`, `.path()`
  (`herogpui/icons/lucide/<name>.svg`), `.svg()` (the embedded bytes),
  `IconName::from_name(..)` / `from_path(..)`, and `From<IconName> for
  SharedString`, so every builder that takes an icon path takes a name
  (`TreeItem::icon(IconName::Folder)`, `svg().path(IconName::X)`).
  `HeroGpuiAssets` serves them with no setup. The set is listed in
  `.shots/lucide-icons.txt` (pinned version and tarball integrity);
  `python3 .shots/sync-lucide.py` copies the listed icons and regenerates
  `IconName`, `--check` verifies list, files and enum offline. The
  gallery's Icons page (Getting Started) is a searchable grid of every
  name. Decorative: no accessibility node (lucide-react marks its svg
  `aria-hidden`). Lucide is ISC (some
  icons MIT via Feather); the license ships in `assets/lucide/LICENSE`.
- **Table data extras** — column reordering: `Table::allows_column_reorder(
  true).on_column_move(|m: &ColumnMove, w, cx| ..)` with `column_order([..])`
  (controlled) or `default_column_order([..])`; orders are indices into the
  columns as given. Drag a header onto another column's place, or Alt+Left
  / Alt+Right on a focused header (the focus follows the column); cells,
  resized and measured widths and the tree column move with it. `ColumnMove
  { from, to, order }` uses display positions for `from`/`to`. Cell
  selection: `cell_selectable(true).on_cell_select(|cell: &TableCell, w, cx|
  ..)` with `selected_cell(Some(TableCell::new(row_key, column)))`
  (controlled) or `default_selected_cell(..)`; `column` is the given index,
  so a cell keeps its identity across moves. A press selects a cell,
  Left/Right/Home/End move within the row, and the row keys (Up/Down,
  PageUp/PageDown, Ctrl+Home/End) keep the column. The selected cell carries
  an inset ring and `aria-selected`. Freeze leading columns with
  `TableColumn::frozen(true)`: frozen columns are displayed first in their
  relative order, followed by scrolling columns; the selection column stays
  fixed too. A column move stays within its frozen or scrolling region.
  Horizontal wheel and trackpad input over either part scrolls the header and
  body together; keyboard cell navigation reveals an offscreen cell. When
  every column is frozen, the table uses its ordinary unsplit layout.
- **Toolbar extras** — `Toolbar::new().size(Size::Sm).sized_child(Button::new(
  id).label(..)).sized_children([..]).label("Formatting")`: `size` reaches
  every `sized_child` (any `Sizable<Size = Size>` control) at render time,
  in any builder order; `child` elements keep their own size. `label` is
  the toolbar's (or nested group's) accessible name, reported with an
  `.id(..)`.
- **TitleBar / WindowBorder** — open the window with
  `TitleBar::window_options()` (or `TitleBar::titlebar_options()` plus
  `app_owns_titlebar_drag: true`), then render
  `WindowBorder::new().child(TitleBar::new(id).title(text).child(el)
  .height(px).controls(TitleBarControls::{Auto, Custom, Hidden})
  .on_window_action(|action: &WindowAction, window, cx| ..))` at the top of
  the root view. The empty bar drags the window and a double-click zooms;
  children keep their presses. `Auto`: macOS keeps the native traffic
  lights (80px `TRAFFIC_LIGHTS_WIDTH` reserved); Windows draws buttons the
  OS performs (`WindowControlArea::{Min, Max, Close}`, not reported to the
  hook); Linux draws buttons only when client-decorated; the web draws
  none. `Custom` draws minimize, maximize/restore and close everywhere.
  `WindowAction::{Minimize, Zoom, Close, Move, DoubleClick,
  ShowWindowMenu(point)}`; the hook replaces `action.perform(window)`.
  `WindowBorder` draws a Linux client-decorated frame (shadow
  `WINDOW_SHADOW_SIZE`, border, resize edges) and is a pass-through
  elsewhere. Roles: `TitleBar` named by the title, `Button` per control.
- **Sidebar** — `Sidebar::new(id, vec![SidebarGroup::new(key).label(text)
  .is_collapsible(bool).default_expanded(bool).items(vec![SidebarItem::new(
  key, label).icon(IconName::Inbox).badge("12").is_disabled(bool), ..]),
  ..]).header(el).footer(el).label(name).width(px(256.))
  .collapsed_width(px(56.)).show_collapse_toggle(bool).is_disabled(bool)
  .on_select(|key, w, cx| ..)`; `.active_key(Some(key))` (controlled) or
  `.default_active_key(key)`; `.is_collapsed(bool)` +
  `.on_collapsed_change(|c: &bool, w, cx| ..)` or `.default_collapsed(bool)`;
  `.expanded_keys([..])` + `.on_expanded_change(|&HashSet<SharedString>, w,
  cx| ..)`. A labelled collapsible group's heading toggles its items
  (Disclosure motion). One tab stop: Up/Down/Home/End over items and
  collapsible headings, Right/Left expand/collapse from a heading,
  Enter/Space activate, typeahead. Collapsed: icons only, group headings
  hidden, each item named by a right-hand `Tooltip` (hover and keyboard
  focus). Fixed pixel widths; for a draggable width put it in a
  `ResizablePanelGroup` panel. Roles: `Navigation`, `Group`, `Button` +
  expanded, `Link`.
- **CommandPalette** — `CommandPalette::new(id, vec![CommandItem::new(key,
  label).group(name).description(text).icon(IconName::File).shortcut(["⌘",
  "N"]).keywords([..]).is_disabled(bool), ..]).on_select(|key, w, cx| ..)
  .placeholder(text).empty_text(text).label(name).width(px)
  .max_list_height(px).close_on_select(bool).filter(|item, query| bool)`;
  `.is_open(bool)` + `.on_open_change(|open: &bool, w, cx| ..)` or
  `.default_open(bool)`. A modal dialog on the overlay stack: the search
  field takes the focus, Tab stays inside, Escape or an outside press closes
  and the focus returns. Default search: every query word must occur
  (case/accent-insensitive) in the label, a keyword or the group. Commands
  keep their order under group headings; Up/Down wrap over enabled
  commands, a new query highlights the first match, Enter or a press runs
  one. Shortcuts are display-only `Kbd`s. Bind Cmd-K/Ctrl-K yourself:
  `is_command_palette_shortcut(&event.keystroke, cx)` in a root `on_key_down`,
  or a GPUI action on `"secondary-k"`. Roles: `Dialog`, `ListBox`,
  `ListBoxOption` (highlight selected, active descendant).
- **HoverCard** — `HoverCard::new(id).content(|w, cx| el.into_any_element())
  .label(name).child(trigger).placement(Placement::Bottom).offset(px)
  .open_delay(ms).close_delay(ms).width(px).radius(px).is_disabled(bool)
  .on_open_change(|open: &bool, w, cx| ..)`; `.is_open(bool)` makes it
  controlled, `.default_open(bool)` seeds it. Hovering the trigger opens
  the card after `open_delay` (`HOVER_CARD_OPEN_DELAY_MS`, 700); keyboard
  focus inside the trigger opens it at once. Leaving the trigger starts
  `close_delay` (`HOVER_CARD_CLOSE_DELAY_MS`, 300), which the pointer
  reaching the card cancels; leaving the card starts it again. Escape (from
  anywhere while it is the topmost overlay), a press outside, or the focus
  leaving the trigger close it. Role: `Group` named by `label` (not a
  tooltip).

## Gallery

`cargo run -p herogpui-gallery` — 1280×820 window, centred. `HEROGPUI_PAGE`
selects the page by nav title, `HEROGPUI_THEME=dark` selects the appearance,
`HEROGPUI_WINDOW_SIZE=1200x2000` sets the window size,
`HEROGPUI_UNFOCUSED=1` opens without taking focus,
`HEROGPUI_THEME_DIR=<dir>` loads and live-reloads the theme files there, and
`HEROGPUI_REDUCE_MOTION=1` turns on the reduced-motion preference at startup
(the gallery calls `theme::set_reduce_motion`; see `gallery/src/main.rs`). The navbar's theme picker switches live between
the light and dark bases and every `presets::PRESETS` theme. Screenshots are the visual regression source.

## Code style

Components and builder types are `#[must_use]`: always pass the built value
on (`.child(..)`, return it from `render`, `.build()` a `ThemeBuilder`,
`.push(cx)` a `Toast`); a dropped chain is an `unused_must_use` warning.

Pinned GPUI notes: `f32::from(px)` for `Pixels`, no `select_none`, `on_click`
and `.active()` need `.id()`, `svg()` never inherits text color, `Arc` for
shared callbacks, `.into_any_element()` for branch unification. Theme tokens are
already `Hsla` — never wrap them in `Hsla::from`. Divs are `Display::Block`, so
put controls in a flex parent or they stretch. Floating panels need GPUI's
`deferred(..)` to paint above later siblings. See `AGENTS.md`.

## Animation

v3 drives motion from data attributes; `crates/herogpui-components/src/anim.rs`
is the gpui equivalent and the single place the timings live.

- `anim::entering(el, id, cx)` — the `[data-entering]` 200ms ease-out fade, used
  by every overlay (Modal, Drawer, AlertDialog, Popover, Dropdown, Select,
  ComboBox, ColorPicker, Toast).
- `anim::entering_from(el, id, edge, travel, cx)` — adds the slide `Drawer` uses.
- `anim::pressed(el, PressBox { .. }, cx)` — v3's `[data-pressed]`
  `scale(0.97)`, applied by `Button` and `ToggleButton`, the two components v3
  documents it for.
- `anim::entering_zoom(el, id, ZoomBox { .. }, cx)` — v3's `[data-entering]` in
  full: `zoom-in-90 fade-in-0 duration-200`. Used by every overlay; the backdrop
  fades alongside it.
- `anim::exiting(el, id, ZoomBox, cx)` / `exiting_to(..)` — v3's
  `[data-exiting]`: `animate-out zoom-out-95 fade-out duration-150`, and the
  drawer's `slide-out-to-*`. A `RenderOnce` component leaves the tree the moment
  `isOpen` goes false, so each overlay holds itself for `EXITING_MS` first
  (`Closed` / `Open` / `Exiting`) and picks the animation.
- `anim::hover_fade(el, id, idle, hovered, hover_border, window, cx)` — v3's
  `transition-colors`. gpui has no property transitions, so the element keeps its
  own hover flag and generation counter and each change eases the fill in OKLab.
  The helper owns the element's one gpui hover style: pass the immediate border
  endpoint as `hover_border` rather than calling `.hover(..)` on the same element
  yourself. That style is what makes gpui notify on a real pointer crossing —
  the fade's own listener records the pointer without notifying, because
  notifying there re-renders forever whenever the element's id is not stable
  across frames.
- `anim::caret_blink(el, id, cx)` — v3's `@keyframes caret-blink`, on the text
  and OTP carets.
- `anim::Motion` — the duration, scale and `Curve` v3 declares per overlay:
  `PANEL_IN` (250ms `ease-out-quad`, from **1.05** — a modal settles *down* onto
  the page), `BACKDROP_IN` (150ms `ease-out`, fade only), `POPOVER_IN` (150ms
  `ease-smooth`, 0.90), `LIST_IN` (150ms, 0.95), `FLUID_IN` (250ms
  `ease-out-fluid`, 0.95), `DRAWER_IN`/`DRAWER_OUT` (250/200ms `ease-out-fluid`),
  and a `*_OUT` for each at 100ms. `anim::Curve` evaluates v3's `--ease-*`
  cubic-beziers exactly, rather than substituting one of gpui's two built-ins.
- `anim::ENTERING_MS` (150), `EXITING_MS` (100), `TRANSITION_MS` (100),
  `PRESS_MS` (250 — recorded, since gpui's `active` has no timeline to ramp
  along), `PRESSED_SCALE`, `anim::pressed_inset`.
- **Reduced motion:** `ActiveTheme::reduce_motion(cx)` gates every animation with no opt-in
  from the caller. Set it with `theme::set_reduce_motion(bool, cx)` or
  `theme::toggle_reduce_motion(cx)` — the only way it is set: the library reads
  no environment variable and GPUI exposes no OS preference, so an app wires it
  to its own settings (the gallery maps `HEROGPUI_REDUCE_MOTION=1` onto it).
  `ThemeProvider::init` leaves the flag as it is. The value is stored in GPUI's own `App::reduce_motion()` global, so a
  plain `gpui::Animation` written by the app is suppressed too, and either
  accessor reads the same flag.

**No div transforms.** the pinned GPUI plumbs `TransformationMatrix` into
`paint_svg` alone, so quads and text cannot be scaled or rotated. Two
consequences — both worked around geometrically rather than left undone:

- The press is **geometric** rather than a transform: `PressBox` scales the
  height, padding, gap, corner radius, minimum width **and type size** by 0.97,
  with margins absorbing exactly what the box gives up, so the outer footprint
  is identical (pressing never nudges a neighbour) while the visible box
  contracts about its centre. Scaling the type is what makes this a real scale
  rather than an inset — gpui accepts fractional font sizes, so the glyphs
  shrink with the box. Two differences from a CSS transform remain: a label
  wider than the control's `min_w` narrows the control by ~3% of that overflow,
  because gpui cannot shrink text without affecting layout; and an icon child
  keeps its size, since its dimensions belong to the caller. `Toast`'s
  `scaleFactor` shrinks stacked toasts the same way, by insetting their width.
- The overlay entry's `zoom-in-90` uses the same technique: `ZoomBox` grows the
  panel's width, padding, type size and corner radius from 90% while it fades
  in. What a real `scale()` would also carry, and this does not, is a child
  whose size the caller fixed — an icon or image inside the panel keeps its
  size while the chrome around it grows.
